sentences.english: As soon as she was small enough to get through the door, she ran out of the house, and found quite a crowd of little animals and birds waiting outside.
sentences.korean: 문으로 들어갈 수 있을 만큼 작아지자마자, 그녀는 집 밖으로 뛰쳐나갔고, 밖에는 꽤 많은 작은 동물과 새들이 기다리고 있는 것을 발견했습니다.

sentences.english: The poor little Lizard, Bill, was in the middle, being held up by two guinea-pigs, who were giving it something out of a bottle.
sentences.korean: 불쌍한 작은 도마뱀 빌은 두 마리의 기니피그에게 들려 가운데에 있었고, 기니피그들은 병에 든 무언가를 빌에게 먹여주고 있었다.

sentences.english: They all made a rush at Alice the moment she appeared; but she ran off as hard as she could, and soon found herself safe in a thick wood.
sentences.korean: 앨리스가 나타나자마자 모두 그녀에게 달려들었지만, 앨리스는 있는 힘껏 도망쳐 곧 울창한 숲 속에서 안전하게 몸을 숨겼습니다.

sentences.english: “The first thing I’ve got to do,” said Alice to herself, as she wandered about in the wood, “is to grow to my right size again; and the second thing is to find my way into that lovely garden.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 숲 속을 거닐며 혼잣말로 "우선 원래 크기로 돌아가야 하고, 두 번째는 저 아름다운 정원으로 가는 길을 찾아야 해."라고 말했다.

sentences.english: I think that will be the best plan.”
sentences.korean: 그게 최선의 계획일 것 같아요.

sentences.english: It sounded an excellent plan, no doubt, and very neatly and simply arranged; the only difficulty was, that she had not the smallest idea how to set about it; and while she was peering about anxiously among the trees, a little sharp bark just over her head made her look up in a great hurry.
sentences.korean: 그 계획은 의심할 여지 없이 훌륭하고 깔끔하며 간단하게 들렸다. 유일한 문제는 그녀가 어떻게 실행해야 할지 전혀 감이 오지 않았다는 것이었다. 그녀가 나무들 사이로 불안하게 주위를 살피고 있을 때, 바로 머리 위에서 날카로운 작은 나무껍질 소리가 들려 그녀는 황급히 고개를 들었다.

sentences.english: An enormous puppy was looking down at her with large round eyes, and feebly stretching out one paw, trying to touch her.
sentences.korean: 커다란 강아지 한 마리가 동그란 눈으로 그녀를 내려다보며, 힘없이 앞발 하나를 뻗어 그녀를 만지려 애쓰고 있었다.

sentences.english: “Poor little thing!”
sentences.korean: "불쌍한 꼬맹이!"

sentences.english: said Alice, in a coaxing tone, and she tried hard to whistle to it; but she was terribly frightened all the time at the thought that it might be hungry, in which case it would be very likely to eat her up in spite of all her coaxing.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 달래는 듯한 목소리로 말하며 휘파람을 불려고 애썼지만, 혹시라도 괴물이 배고플까 봐, 아무리 달래도 잡아먹힐까 봐 계속 겁에 질렸다.

sentences.english: Hardly knowing what she did, she picked up a little bit of stick, and held it out to the puppy; whereupon the puppy jumped into the air off all its feet at once, with a yelp of delight, and rushed at the stick, and made believe to worry it; then Alice dodged behind a great thistle, to keep herself from being run over; and the moment she appeared on the other side, the puppy made another rush at the stick, and tumbled head over heels in its hurry to get hold of it; then Alice, thinking it was very like having a game of play with a cart-horse, and expecting every moment to be trampled under its feet, ran round the thistle again; then the puppy began a series of short charges at the stick, running a very little way forwards each time and a long way back, and barking hoarsely all the while, till at last it sat down a good way off, panting, with its tongue hanging out of its mouth, and its great eyes half shut.
sentences.korean: 무슨 짓을 하는지도 모른 채, 앨리스는 작은 나뭇가지를 주워 강아지에게 내밀었습니다. 그러자 강아지는 기쁨에 찬 낑낑거림과 함께 네 발로 껑충 뛰어올라 나뭇가지를 향해 달려들며 장난을 쳤습니다. 앨리스는 강아지에게 밟히지 않으려고 커다란 엉겅퀴 뒤로 숨었습니다. 앨리스가 엉겅퀴 너머로 모습을 드러내자마자, 강아지는 다시 나뭇가지를 향해 달려들었고, 그것을 잡으려다 엉덩방아를 찧었습니다. 앨리스는 마치 마차를 끄는 말과 노는 것 같다는 생각에, 언제라도 밟힐 것 같은 불안감에 엉겅퀴 주위를 다시 뛰어갔습니다. 그러자 강아지는 나뭇가지를 향해 짧게 돌진했다가 멀리 되돌아오기를 반복하며 쉰 목소리로 짖어댔습니다. 마침내 강아지는 꽤 떨어진 곳에 주저앉아 헐떡이며 혀를 내밀고 커다란 눈을 반쯤 감았습니다.

sentences.english: This seemed to Alice a good opportunity for making her escape; so she set off at once, and ran till she was quite tired and out of breath, and till the puppy’s bark sounded quite faint in the distance.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 이것이 탈출할 절호의 기회라고 생각했습니다. 그래서 곧바로 출발하여 숨이 턱까지 차오를 때까지, 그리고 멀리서 강아지 짖는 소리가 희미하게 들릴 때까지 달렸습니다.

sentences.english: “And yet what a dear little puppy it was!”
sentences.korean: "그런데도 얼마나 사랑스러운 강아지였던가!"

sentences.english: said Alice, as she leant against a buttercup to rest herself, and fanned herself with one of the leaves: “I should have liked teaching it tricks very much, if—if I’d only been the right size to do it!
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 미나리아재비에 기대어 쉬면서 잎사귀 하나로 부채질을 하며 말했다. "내가 만약, 만약 몸집만 맞았더라면, 얘한테 재주를 가르쳐주는 걸 정말 좋아했을 텐데!"

sentences.english: Oh dear!
sentences.korean: 이런!

sentences.english: I’d nearly forgotten that I’ve got to grow up again!
sentences.korean: 내가 다시 어른이 되어야 한다는 사실을 거의 잊을 뻔했어!

sentences.english: Let me see—how is it to be managed?
sentences.korean: 음, 어떻게 관리해야 할까요?

sentences.english: I suppose I ought to eat or drink something or other; but the great question is, what?”
sentences.korean: 아무래도 뭐라도 먹거나 마셔야 할 것 같은데, 문제는 뭘 먹어야 할까 하는 거야.

sentences.english: The great question certainly was, what?
sentences.korean: 가장 중요한 질문은 바로 "무엇인가?"였습니다.

sentences.english: Alice looked all round her at the flowers and the blades of grass, but she did not see anything that looked like the right thing to eat or drink under the circumstances.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 주위의 꽃과 풀들을 샅샅이 살펴보았지만, 지금 상황에서 먹거나 마실 만한 것은 아무것도 보이지 않았다.

sentences.english: There was a large mushroom growing near her, about the same height as herself; and when she had looked under it, and on both sides of it, and behind it, it occurred to her that she might as well look and see what was on the top of it.
sentences.korean: 그녀 근처에는 그녀 키와 거의 같은 커다란 버섯이 자라고 있었다. 그녀는 버섯 아래와 양옆, 그리고 뒤쪽까지 살펴본 후, 버섯 꼭대기에는 무엇이 있는지 한번 살펴보는 것도 좋겠다는 생각이 들었다.

sentences.english: She stretched herself up on tiptoe, and peeped over the edge of the mushroom, and her eyes immediately met those of a large blue caterpillar, that was sitting on the top with its arms folded, quietly smoking a long hookah, and taking not the smallest notice of her or of anything else.
sentences.korean: 그녀는 발끝으로 서서 버섯 꼭대기 너머로 살짝 고개를 내밀었고, 곧바로 팔짱을 끼고 버섯 꼭대기에 앉아 긴 물담배를 조용히 피우고 있는 커다란 파란색 애벌레와 눈이 마주쳤다. 애벌레는 그녀나 다른 어떤 것에도 조금도 신경 쓰지 않는 듯했다.

sentences.english: The Caterpillar and Alice looked at each other for some time in silence: at last the Caterpillar took the hookah out of its mouth, and addressed her in a languid, sleepy voice.
sentences.korean: 애벌레와 앨리스는 한동안 말없이 서로를 바라보았다. 마침내 애벌레는 입에서 물담배를 빼고 나른하고 졸린 목소리로 앨리스에게 말을 걸었다.

sentences.english: “Who are you?”
sentences.korean: "누구세요?"

sentences.english: said the Caterpillar.
sentences.korean: 캐터필러 측은 이렇게 말했다.

sentences.english: This was not an encouraging opening for a conversation.
sentences.korean: 이는 대화를 시작하기에 좋은 분위기가 아니었다.

sentences.english: Alice replied, rather shyly, “I—I hardly know, sir, just at present—at least I know who I was when I got up this morning, but I think I must have been changed several times since then.”
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 다소 수줍게 대답했다. "저는... 솔직히 잘 모르겠어요, 선생님. 적어도 오늘 아침에 일어났을 때 제가 누구였는지는 알겠는데, 그 이후로 여러 번 바뀐 것 같아요."

sentences.english: “What do you mean by that?”
sentences.korean: 그게 무슨 뜻이에요?

sentences.english: said the Caterpillar sternly.
sentences.korean: 캐터필러가 엄하게 말했다.

sentences.english: “Explain yourself!”
sentences.korean: “설명해 보세요!”

sentences.english: “I can’t explain myself, I’m afraid, sir,” said Alice, “because I’m not myself, you see.”
sentences.korean: "죄송하지만 제 심정을 설명해 드릴 수가 없네요, 선생님." 앨리스가 말했다. "왜냐하면 저는 지금 제 자신이 아니거든요."

sentences.english: “I don’t see,” said the Caterpillar.
sentences.korean: "안 보여요."라고 캐터필러가 말했다.

sentences.english: “I’m afraid I can’t put it more clearly,” Alice replied very politely, “for I can’t understand it myself to begin with; and being so many different sizes in a day is very confusing.”
sentences.korean: "죄송하지만 더 자세히 설명해 드릴 수가 없네요." 앨리스는 아주 정중하게 대답했다. "저도 처음에는 잘 이해가 안 되고, 하루 동안 여러 가지 모습으로 변하는 건 정말 혼란스러워요."

sentences.english: “It isn’t,” said the Caterpillar.
sentences.korean: "그렇지 않아요."라고 캐터필러가 말했다.

sentences.english: “Well, perhaps you haven’t found it so yet,” said Alice; “but when you have to turn into a chrysalis—you will some day, you know—and then after that into a butterfly, I should think you’ll feel it a little queer, won’t you?”
sentences.korean: "글쎄, 아직은 그렇게 느끼지 못했을지도 몰라." 앨리스가 말했다. "하지만 언젠가는 번데기가 되고, 그 후에 나비가 되면, 그때는 좀 이상한 기분이 들지 않을까?"

sentences.english: “Not a bit,” said the Caterpillar.
sentences.korean: "전혀 그렇지 않아요."라고 캐터필러가 말했다.

sentences.english: “Well, perhaps your feelings may be different,” said Alice; “all I know is, it would feel very queer to me.”
sentences.korean: "글쎄요, 당신의 생각은 다를 수도 있겠죠." 앨리스가 말했다. "제가 아는 건, 제겐 굉장히 이상하게 느껴질 거라는 거예요."

sentences.english: “You!”
said the Caterpillar contemptuously.
sentences.korean: 캐터필러는 경멸적으로 말했다.

sentences.english: “Who are you?”
sentences.korean: "누구세요?"

sentences.english: Which brought them back again to the beginning of the conversation.
sentences.korean: 그렇게 해서 그들은 다시 대화의 처음으로 돌아갔다.

sentences.english: Alice felt a little irritated at the Caterpillar’s making such very short remarks, and she drew herself up and said, very gravely, “I think, you ought to tell me who you are, first.”
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 애벌레가 너무 짧게 말하는 것에 약간 짜증이 나서 자세를 바로잡고 아주 진지한 표정으로 말했다. "제 생각에는, 먼저 당신이 누구인지 말해줘야 할 것 같아요."

sentences.english: “Why?”
said the Caterpillar.
sentences.korean: 캐터필러 측은 이렇게 말했다.

sentences.english: Here was another puzzling question; and as Alice could not think of any good reason, and as the Caterpillar seemed to be in a very unpleasant state of mind, she turned away.
sentences.korean: 이것 또한 당혹스러운 질문이었다. 앨리스는 마땅한 이유를 떠올릴 수 없었고, 애벌레의 기분도 매우 좋지 않아 보였기에, 그녀는 고개를 돌렸다.

sentences.english: “Come back!”
sentences.korean: “돌아와!”

sentences.english: the Caterpillar called after her.
sentences.korean: 애벌레가 그녀를 불렀다.

sentences.english: “I’ve something important to say!”
sentences.korean: “제가 할 말이 있어요!”

sentences.english: This sounded promising, certainly: Alice turned and came back again.
sentences.korean: 이것은 분명 희망적인 것처럼 들렸다. 앨리스는 돌아서서 다시 돌아왔다.

sentences.english: “Keep your temper,” said the Caterpillar.
sentences.korean: "화내지 마,"라고 캐터필러가 말했다.

sentences.english: “Is that all?”
sentences.korean: “그게 다예요?”

sentences.english: said Alice, swallowing down her anger as well as she could.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 최대한 분노를 억누르며 말했다.

sentences.english: “No,” said the Caterpillar.
sentences.korean: "아니요,"라고 캐터필러가 말했다.

sentences.english: Alice thought she might as well wait, as she had nothing else to do, and perhaps after all it might tell her something worth hearing.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 어차피 할 일도 없으니 기다려보는 게 낫겠다고 생각했고, 어쩌면 그 과정에서 들을 만한 가치 있는 이야기를 들을 수 있을지도 모른다고 여겼다.

sentences.english: For some minutes it puffed away without speaking, but at last it unfolded its arms, took the hookah out of its mouth again, and said, “So you think you’re changed, do you?”
sentences.korean: 몇 분 동안 아무 말도 없이 담배 연기를 뿜어대더니, 마침내 팔을 펴고 입에서 물담배를 다시 빼내더니 “네가 변했다고 생각하는 거냐?”라고 말했다.

sentences.english: “I’m afraid I am, sir,” said Alice; “I can’t remember things as I used—and I don’t keep the same size for ten minutes together!”
sentences.korean: "아무래도 그런 것 같아요, 선생님." 앨리스가 말했다. "예전처럼 기억력이 좋지 않고, 10분도 채 안 돼서 몸 상태가 일정하지 않아요!"

sentences.english: “Can’t remember what things?”
sentences.korean: "무슨 것들인지 기억이 안 나세요?"

sentences.english: said the Caterpillar.
sentences.korean: 캐터필러 측은 이렇게 말했다.

sentences.english: “Well, I’ve tried to say “How doth the little busy bee,” but it all came different!”
sentences.korean: "음, '부지런한 작은 꿀벌은 어떻게 지내니?'라고 말하려고 했는데, 전혀 다르게 나왔어요!"

sentences.english: Alice replied in a very melancholy voice.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 매우 슬픈 목소리로 대답했다.

sentences.english: “Repeat, ‘You are old, Father William,’” said the Caterpillar.
sentences.korean: "다시 한번, '윌리엄 신부님, 늙으셨잖아요'라고 말해 보세요."라고 애벌레가 말했다.

sentences.english: Alice folded her hands, and began:—
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 두 손을 모으고 말을 시작했다.

sentences.english: “You are old, Father William,” the young man said, “And your hair has become very white; And yet you incessantly stand on your head— Do you think, at your age, it is right?”
sentences.korean: "윌리엄 신부님, 나이가 많으시고 머리카락도 하얗게 세셨는데, 끊임없이 물구나무를 서 계시잖아요. 이 나이에 그렇게 하시는 게 옳다고 생각하세요?" 젊은이가 말했다.

sentences.english: “In my youth,” Father William replied to his son, “I feared it might injure the brain; But, now that I’m perfectly sure I have none, Why, I do it again and again.”
sentences.korean: "젊었을 때는 뇌에 해로울까 봐 두려웠지." 윌리엄 아버지가 아들에게 대답했다. "하지만 이제 내 뇌가 전혀 없다는 걸 확신하니, 뭐, 계속해서 반복하는 거지."

sentences.english: “You are old,” said the youth, “as I mentioned before, And have grown most uncommonly fat; Yet you turned a back-somersault in at the door— Pray, what is the reason of that?”
sentences.korean: “당신은 나이가 많으시고,” 젊은이가 말했다. “전에 말씀드렸듯이, 몸도 몹시 뚱뚱해지셨는데, 문 앞에서 공중제비를 돌며 들어오셨군요. 도대체 무슨 이유입니까?”

sentences.english: “In my youth,” said the sage, as he shook his grey locks, “I kept all my limbs very supple By the use of this ointment—one shilling the box— Allow me to sell you a couple?”
sentences.korean: "젊었을 때," 현자는 백발을 흔들며 말했다. "이 연고를 써서 온몸을 아주 유연하게 유지했지. 한 상자에 1실링인데, 두 상자 사시겠나?"

sentences.english: “You are old,” said the youth, “and your jaws are too weak For anything tougher than suet; Yet you finished the goose, with the bones and the beak— Pray, how did you manage to do it?”
sentences.korean: 젊은이가 말했다. "당신은 늙었고, 턱이 너무 약해서 양지방보다 질긴 것은 먹을 수 없을 텐데, 뼈와 부리까지 남김없이 거위를 다 드셨잖아요. 도대체 어떻게 하신 겁니까?"

sentences.english: “In my youth,” said his father, “I took to the law, And argued each case with my wife; And the muscular strength, which it gave to my jaw, Has lasted the rest of my life.”
sentences.korean: "젊었을 때 나는 법률을 공부했고, 아내와 함께 사건 하나하나를 논쟁했지. 그때 길러진 턱 근육이 평생 동안 유지되었단다."라고 그의 아버지가 말했다.

sentences.english: “You are old,” said the youth, “one would hardly suppose That your eye was as steady as ever; Yet you balanced an eel on the end of your nose— What made you so awfully clever?”
sentences.korean: 젊은이가 말했다. "당신은 나이가 많으신데, 눈썰미가 예전처럼 또렷하실 거라고는 생각하기 어렵군요. 그런데도 코끝에 장어를 올려놓으셨으니, 도대체 어떻게 그렇게 영리하신 겁니까?"

sentences.english: “I have answered three questions, and that is enough,” Said his father; “don’t give yourself airs!
sentences.korean: "질문 세 개에 대답했으니 그걸로 충분하다." 아버지가 말했다. "잘난 척하지 마라!"

sentences.english: Do you think I can listen all day to such stuff?
sentences.korean: 내가 그런 걸 하루 종일 들을 수 있을 거라고 생각하세요?

sentences.english: Be off, or I’ll kick you down stairs!”
sentences.korean: 당장 꺼져! 안 그러면 계단 아래로 차버릴 거야!

sentences.english: “That is not said right,” said the Caterpillar.
sentences.korean: 캐터필러 측은 "그건 잘못된 표현입니다."라고 말했다.

sentences.english: “Not quite right, I’m afraid,” said Alice, timidly; “some of the words have got altered.”
sentences.korean: "아쉽게도 완전히 정확하지는 않아요." 앨리스가 조심스럽게 말했다. "단어 몇 개가 바뀌었어요."

sentences.english: “It is wrong from beginning to end,” said the Caterpillar decidedly, and there was silence for some minutes.
sentences.korean: "처음부터 끝까지 다 틀렸어." 캐터필러가 단호하게 말했고, 몇 분 동안 침묵이 흘렀다.

sentences.english: The Caterpillar was the first to speak.
sentences.korean: 캐터필러가 먼저 말을 꺼냈다.

sentences.english: “What size do you want to be?”
sentences.korean: "어떤 사이즈를 원하세요?"

sentences.english: it asked.
sentences.korean: 그것이 물었다.

sentences.english: “Oh, I’m not particular as to size,” Alice hastily replied; “only one doesn’t like changing so often, you know.”
sentences.korean: "아, 사이즈는 별로 신경 안 써요." 앨리스가 황급히 대답했다. "다만, 너무 자주 갈아입는 건 싫거든요."

sentences.english: “I don’t know,” said the Caterpillar.
sentences.korean: "모르겠어요."라고 캐터필러가 말했다.

sentences.english: Alice said nothing: she had never been so much contradicted in her life before, and she felt that she was losing her temper.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 아무 말도 하지 않았다. 그녀는 살면서 이렇게까지 반박을 받아본 적이 없었고, 화가 치밀어 오르는 것 같았다.

sentences.english: “Are you content now?”
sentences.korean: "지금 만족하시나요?"

sentences.english: said the Caterpillar.
sentences.korean: 캐터필러 측은 이렇게 말했다.

sentences.english: “Well, I should like to be a little larger, sir, if you wouldn’t mind,” said Alice: “three inches is such a wretched height to be.”
sentences.korean: "선생님, 괜찮으시다면 제가 조금 더 컸으면 좋겠어요. 3인치는 너무 작은 키잖아요." 앨리스가 말했다.

sentences.english: “It is a very good height indeed!”
sentences.korean: "정말 적당한 높이네요!"

sentences.english: said the Caterpillar angrily, rearing itself upright as it spoke (it was exactly three inches high).
sentences.korean: 캐터필러는 화난 듯이 말하며 몸을 똑바로 세웠다(키는 정확히 3인치였다).

sentences.english: “But I’m not used to it!”
sentences.korean: 하지만 저는 그런 상황에 익숙하지 않아요!

sentences.english: pleaded poor Alice in a piteous tone.
sentences.korean: 불쌍한 앨리스는 애처로운 어조로 간청했다.

sentences.english: And she thought of herself, “I wish the creatures wouldn’t be so easily offended!”
sentences.korean: 그리고 그녀는 속으로 생각했다. "저 생물들이 그렇게 쉽게 기분 상하지 않았으면 좋겠어!"

sentences.english: “You’ll get used to it in time,” said the Caterpillar; and it put the hookah into its mouth and began smoking again.
sentences.korean: "시간이 지나면 익숙해질 거야." 애벌레가 말하며 물담배를 입에 물고 다시 피우기 시작했다.

sentences.english: This time Alice waited patiently until it chose to speak again.
sentences.korean: 이번에는 앨리스가 그것이 다시 말을 할 때까지 참을성 있게 기다렸다.

sentences.english: In a minute or two the Caterpillar took the hookah out of its mouth and yawned once or twice, and shook itself.
sentences.korean: 1, 2분쯤 지나자 애벌레는 입에서 물담배를 빼고 하품을 한두 번 한 다음 몸을 털었다.

sentences.english: Then it got down off the mushroom, and crawled away in the grass, merely remarking as it went, “One side will make you grow taller, and the other side will make you grow shorter.”
sentences.korean: 그러자 그것은 버섯에서 내려와 풀밭으로 기어가면서 "한쪽은 키를 크게 해주고, 다른 쪽은 키를 작게 해줄 거야."라고 한마디만 남겼다.

sentences.english: “One side of what?
sentences.korean: "무엇의 한쪽 편을 말씀하시는 거죠?"

sentences.english: The other side of what?”
sentences.korean: 무엇의 반대편이라는 거죠?

sentences.english: thought Alice to herself.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 속으로 생각했다.

sentences.english: “Of the mushroom,” said the Caterpillar, just as if she had asked it aloud; and in another moment it was out of sight.
sentences.korean: 애벌레는 마치 소리 내어 묻는 것처럼 "버섯 말이야."라고 대답했고, 순식간에 시야에서 사라졌다.

sentences.english: Alice remained looking thoughtfully at the mushroom for a minute, trying to make out which were the two sides of it; and as it was perfectly round, she found this a very difficult question.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 버섯을 잠시 동안 생각에 잠긴 듯 바라보며 어느 쪽이 양면인지 알아내려고 애썼다. 버섯이 완벽하게 둥글었기에, 그녀는 그것이 매우 어려운 문제라는 것을 깨달았다.

sentences.english: However, at last she stretched her arms round it as far as they would go, and broke off a bit of the edge with each hand.
sentences.korean: 그러나 마침내 그녀는 팔을 최대한 뻗어 그것을 감싸 쥐었고, 양손으로 가장자리를 조금씩 부러뜨렸다.

sentences.english: “And now which is which?”
sentences.korean: “그럼 이제 어느 쪽이 어느 쪽일까요?”

sentences.english: she said to herself, and nibbled a little of the right-hand bit to try the effect: the next moment she felt a violent blow underneath her chin: it had struck her foot!
sentences.korean: 그녀는 속으로 생각하며 효과를 시험해 보려고 오른쪽 부분을 조금 깨물어 보았다. 바로 그때 턱 아래에 강한 충격이 느껴졌다. 발에 맞은 것이었다!

sentences.english: She was a good deal frightened by this very sudden change, but she felt that there was no time to be lost, as she was shrinking rapidly; so she set to work at once to eat some of the other bit.
sentences.korean: 그녀는 이 갑작스러운 변화에 몹시 겁을 먹었지만, 몸이 빠르게 줄어들고 있었기에 더 이상 시간을 지체할 수 없다고 생각했습니다. 그래서 곧바로 남은 부분을 먹기 시작했습니다.

sentences.english: Her chin was pressed so closely against her foot, that there was hardly room to open her mouth; but she did it at last, and managed to swallow a morsel of the lefthand bit.
sentences.korean: 그녀는 턱을 발에 바짝 붙인 탓에 입을 벌릴 공간조차 거의 없었지만, 마침내 입을 벌려 왼쪽 재갈의 일부를 삼킬 수 있었다.

sentences.english: “Come, my head’s free at last!”
sentences.korean: "자, 드디어 내 머리가 자유로워졌어!"

sentences.english: said Alice in a tone of delight, which changed into alarm in another moment, when she found that her shoulders were nowhere to be found: all she could see, when she looked down, was an immense length of neck, which seemed to rise like a stalk out of a sea of green leaves that lay far below her.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 기쁨에 찬 목소리로 말했지만, 곧 어깨가 사라진 것을 발견하고는 놀라움으로 바뀌었다. 아래를 내려다보니 푸른 잎사귀 바다에서 줄기처럼 솟아오른 거대한 목만 보였다.

sentences.english: “What can all that green stuff be?”
sentences.korean: “저 초록색 물질들은 다 뭘까?”

sentences.english: said Alice.
sentences.korean: 앨리스가 말했다.

sentences.english: “And where have my shoulders got to?
sentences.korean: “그런데 내 어깨는 어디로 갔지?”

sentences.english: And oh, my poor hands, how is it I can’t see you?”
sentences.korean: 아, 불쌍한 내 손아, 어째서 너를 볼 수 없는 걸까?

sentences.english: She was moving them about as she spoke, but no result seemed to follow, except a little shaking among the distant green leaves.
sentences.korean: 그녀는 말을 하면서 그것들을 이리저리 움직였지만, 멀리 있는 초록 잎사귀들 사이에서 약간의 흔들림 외에는 아무런 변화도 없는 듯했다.

sentences.english: As there seemed to be no chance of getting her hands up to her head, she tried to get her head down to them, and was delighted to find that her neck would bend about easily in any direction, like a serpent.
sentences.korean: 손을 머리 위로 올릴 방법이 없어 보이자, 그녀는 머리를 아래로 숙여 손을 머리 위로 올리려 했고, 마치 뱀처럼 목이 어느 방향으로든 쉽게 구부러지는 것을 발견하고 기뻐했다.

sentences.english: She had just succeeded in curving it down into a graceful zigzag, and was going to dive in among the leaves, which she found to be nothing but the tops of the trees under which she had been wandering, when a sharp hiss made her draw back in a hurry: a large pigeon had flown into her face, and was beating her violently with its wings.
sentences.korean: 그녀는 간신히 나뭇잎을 우아한 지그재그 모양으로 휘어지게 조종하는 데 성공했고, 나뭇잎 사이로 뛰어들려고 했지만, 그곳에는 그녀가 헤매던 나무 꼭대기밖에 없었다. 그때 날카로운 쉿 소리가 나더니 그녀는 황급히 뒤로 물러섰다. 커다란 비둘기 한 마리가 그녀의 얼굴로 날아들어 날갯짓으로 사정없이 때리고 있었던 것이다.

sentences.english: “Serpent!”
screamed the Pigeon.
sentences.korean: 비둘기가 비명을 질렀다.

sentences.english: “I’m not a serpent!”
sentences.korean: “나는 뱀이 아니야!”

sentences.english: said Alice indignantly.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 분개하며 말했다.

sentences.english: “Let me alone!”
sentences.korean: “나 좀 내버려 둬!”

sentences.english: “Serpent, I say again!”
sentences.korean: “뱀이라고 다시 말하노라!”

sentences.english: repeated the Pigeon, but in a more subdued tone, and added with a kind of sob, “I’ve tried every way, and nothing seems to suit them!”
sentences.korean: 비둘기는 좀 더 차분한 어조로 같은 말을 반복하며 흐느끼는 듯한 목소리로 덧붙였다. "온갖 방법을 다 써봤지만, 아무 소용이 없더라고요!"

sentences.english: “I haven’t the least idea what you’re talking about,” said Alice.
sentences.korean: “무슨 말씀이신지 전혀 모르겠어요.”라고 앨리스가 말했다.

sentences.english: “I’ve tried the roots of trees, and I’ve tried banks, and I’ve tried hedges,” the Pigeon went on, without attending to her; “but those serpents!
sentences.korean: “나무뿌리도, 둑도, 울타리도 다 가 봤지만,” 비둘기는 그녀의 말을 듣지 않고 계속 말했다. “뱀들은 정말!

sentences.english: There’s no pleasing them!”
sentences.korean: 그들을 만족시킬 방법은 없어요!

sentences.english: Alice was more and more puzzled, but she thought there was no use in saying anything more till the Pigeon had finished.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 점점 더 어리둥절해졌지만, 비둘기가 말을 마칠 때까지 더 이상 아무 말도 하지 않는 것이 좋겠다고 생각했다.

sentences.english: “As if it wasn’t trouble enough hatching the eggs,” said the Pigeon; “but I must be on the look-out for serpents night and day!
sentences.korean: “알을 부화시키는 것만으로도 충분히 힘든데,” 비둘기가 말했다. “밤낮으로 뱀을 경계해야 한다니!”

sentences.english: Why, I haven’t had a wink of sleep these three weeks!”
sentences.korean: 어머, 나 지난 3주 동안 한숨도 못 잤어!

sentences.english: “I’m very sorry you’ve been annoyed,” said Alice, who was beginning to see its meaning.
sentences.korean: "기분 상하셨다니 정말 죄송해요." 앨리스는 그 말의 의미를 조금씩 이해하기 시작하며 말했다.

sentences.english: “And just as I’d taken the highest tree in the wood,” continued the Pigeon, raising its voice to a shriek, “and just as I was thinking I should be free of them at last, they must needs come wriggling down from the sky!
sentences.korean: "내가 숲에서 제일 높은 나무에 올라간 바로 그때," 비둘기는 비명을 지르듯 목소리를 높이며 말을 이었다. "드디어 그들에게서 벗어날 수 있겠다고 생각했는데, 설마 그들이 하늘에서 꿈틀거리며 내려온 건 아니겠지!"

sentences.english: Ugh, Serpent!”
sentences.korean: 으, 뱀이로군!

sentences.english: “But I’m not a serpent, I tell you!”
sentences.korean: “하지만 난 뱀이 아니라고!”

sentences.english: said Alice.
sentences.korean: 앨리스가 말했다.

sentences.english: “I’m a—I’m a—”
sentences.korean: “저는… 저는…”

sentences.english: “Well!
What are you?”
sentences.korean: 당신은 무엇입니까?

sentences.english: said the Pigeon.
sentences.korean: 비둘기가 말했다.

sentences.english: “I can see you’re trying to invent something!”
sentences.korean: "뭔가를 발명하려고 애쓰는 게 보이네요!"

sentences.english: “I—I’m a little girl,” said Alice, rather doubtfully, as she remembered the number of changes she had gone through that day.
sentences.korean: "저는... 저는 어린 소녀예요." 앨리스는 그날 자신이 겪은 수많은 변화를 떠올리며 다소 의심스러운 표정으로 말했다.

sentences.english: “A likely story indeed!”
sentences.korean: "정말 그럴듯한 이야기네요!"

sentences.english: said the Pigeon in a tone of the deepest contempt.
sentences.korean: 비둘기는 극도의 경멸이 담긴 어조로 말했다.

sentences.english: “I’ve seen a good many little girls in my time, but never one with such a neck as that!
sentences.korean: "내가 살면서 많은 어린 소녀들을 봤지만, 저렇게 목이 긴 소녀는 처음 봤어!"

sentences.english: No, no!
sentences.korean: 아니, 아니!

sentences.english: You’re a serpent; and there’s no use denying it.
sentences.korean: 너는 뱀이야. 그걸 부정해봤자 소용없어.

sentences.english: I suppose you’ll be telling me next that you never tasted an egg!”
sentences.korean: 다음엔 계란 맛을 한 번도 못 봤다고 하시겠네요!

sentences.english: “I have tasted eggs, certainly,” said Alice, who was a very truthful child; “but little girls eat eggs quite as much as serpents do, you know.”
sentences.korean: "물론 계란 맛은 봤죠." 아주 정직한 아이였던 앨리스가 말했다. "하지만 아시다시피, 여자아이들은 뱀만큼이나 계란을 많이 먹잖아요."

sentences.english: “I don’t believe it,” said the Pigeon; “but if they do, why then they’re a kind of serpent, that’s all I can say.”
sentences.korean: 비둘기가 말했다. "믿을 수 없지만, 만약 그들이 정말 그렇다면, 그들은 뱀과 같은 존재일 거야. 내가 할 수 있는 말은 그게 전부야."

sentences.english: This was such a new idea to Alice, that she was quite silent for a minute or two, which gave the Pigeon the opportunity of adding, “You’re looking for eggs, I know that well enough; and what does it matter to me whether you’re a little girl or a serpent?”
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 이 생각이 너무나 생소해서 1, 2분 정도 아무 말도 하지 못했는데, 그 틈을 타 비둘기가 말을 덧붙였다. "네가 달걀을 찾고 있다는 건 나도 잘 알아. 그리고 네가 어린 소녀든 뱀이든 나랑 무슨 상관이야?"

sentences.english: “It matters a good deal to me,” said Alice hastily; “but I’m not looking for eggs, as it happens; and if I was, I shouldn’t want yours: I don’t like them raw.”
sentences.korean: "저한테는 아주 중요한 문제예요." 앨리스가 황급히 말했다. "하지만 사실 전 달걀을 찾고 있는 게 아니에요. 설령 찾는다고 해도 당신 달걀은 안 받을 거예요. 전 날달걀을 좋아하지 않거든요."

sentences.english: “Well, be off, then!”
sentences.korean: “그럼, 가보시죠!”

sentences.english: said the Pigeon in a sulky tone, as it settled down again into its nest.
sentences.korean: 비둘기는 뚱한 목소리로 말하며 다시 둥지에 자리를 잡았다.

sentences.english: Alice crouched down among the trees as well as she could, for her neck kept getting entangled among the branches, and every now and then she had to stop and untwist it.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 나무들 사이로 최대한 웅크리고 앉았지만, 목이 자꾸 나뭇가지에 걸려 이따금씩 멈춰 서서 목을 풀어줘야 했다.

sentences.english: After a while she remembered that she still held the pieces of mushroom in her hands, and she set to work very carefully, nibbling first at one and then at the other, and growing sometimes taller and sometimes shorter, until she had succeeded in bringing herself down to her usual height.
sentences.korean: 잠시 후 그녀는 손에 버섯 조각들이 아직 들려 있다는 것을 기억하고는 아주 조심스럽게 하나씩 갉아먹기 시작했다. 때로는 키가 커지고 때로는 작아지기도 하면서 마침내 평소 키로 돌아올 수 있었다.

sentences.english: It was so long since she had been anything near the right size, that it felt quite strange at first; but she got used to it in a few minutes, and began talking to herself, as usual.
sentences.korean: 그녀는 오랫동안 제법 적당한 사이즈였던 적이 없어서 처음에는 꽤 어색했지만, 몇 분 만에 익숙해져서 평소처럼 혼잣말을 하기 시작했다.

sentences.english: “Come, there’s half my plan done now!
sentences.korean: "자, 내 계획의 절반은 이제 끝났어!"

sentences.english: How puzzling all these changes are!
sentences.korean: 이 모든 변화들이 정말 당혹스럽네요!

sentences.english: I’m never sure what I’m going to be, from one minute to another!
sentences.korean: 나는 매 순간 내가 어떤 모습일지 전혀 확신할 수 없어!

sentences.english: However, I’ve got back to my right size: the next thing is, to get into that beautiful garden—how is that to be done, I wonder?”
sentences.korean: 하지만 이제 원래 몸 크기로 돌아왔어요. 다음 목표는 저 아름다운 정원에 들어가는 건데, 어떻게 하면 될까요?

sentences.english: As she said this, she came suddenly upon an open place, with a little house in it about four feet high.
sentences.korean: 그녀가 이렇게 말하는 순간, 갑자기 탁 트인 공간이 나타났는데, 그곳에는 높이가 약 1.2미터 정도 되는 작은 집이 있었다.

sentences.english: “Whoever lives there,” thought Alice, “it’ll never do to come upon them this size: why, I should frighten them out of their wits!”
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 속으로 생각했다. "저기에 누가 살든 간에, 이 크기로 그들을 마주치면 안 될 거야. 내가 나타나면 그들은 완전히 겁에 질려 정신을 잃을지도 몰라!"

sentences.english: So she began nibbling at the righthand bit again, and did not venture to go near the house till she had brought herself down to nine inches high.
sentences.korean: 그래서 그녀는 다시 오른쪽 부분을 조금씩 갉아먹기 시작했고, 몸집이 9인치(약 23cm)까지 줄어들 때까지 집 근처에는 감히 가지 못했다.

sentences.english: For a minute or two she stood looking at the house, and wondering what to do next, when suddenly a footman in livery came running out of the wood—(she considered him to be a footman because he was in livery: otherwise, judging by his face only, she would have called him a fish)—and rapped loudly at the door with his knuckles.
sentences.korean: 그녀는 1, 2분 정도 집을 바라보며 다음에 무엇을 해야 할지 생각하고 있었는데, 그때 갑자기 제복을 입은 하인이 숲에서 뛰쳐나왔다. (그녀는 그가 제복을 입고 있었기 때문에 하인이라고 생각했다. 얼굴만 봤다면 물고기라고 했을 것이다.) 그리고는 손가락 마디로 문을 세게 두드렸다.

sentences.english: It was opened by another footman in livery, with a round face, and large eyes like a frog; and both footmen, Alice noticed, had powdered hair that curled all over their heads.
sentences.korean: 둥근 얼굴에 개구리처럼 큰 눈을 가진, 제복을 입은 또 다른 하인이 문을 열어주었다. 앨리스는 두 하인 모두 머리에 가루를 발라 곱슬머리가 되어 있는 것을 알아챘다.

sentences.english: She felt very curious to know what it was all about, and crept a little way out of the wood to listen.
sentences.korean: 그녀는 그게 도대체 무슨 일인지 너무 궁금해서 숲에서 조금 빠져나와 귀를 기울였다.

sentences.english: The Fish-Footman began by producing from under his arm a great letter, nearly as large as himself, and this he handed over to the other, saying, in a solemn tone, “For the Duchess.
sentences.korean: 물고기 발잡이는 먼저 팔 아래에서 자신만큼이나 큰 편지를 꺼내더니 엄숙한 어조로 "공작부인께."라고 말하며 상대방에게 건넸다.

sentences.english: An invitation from the Queen to play croquet.”
sentences.korean: 여왕께서 크로케 경기를 하자고 초대하셨습니다.

sentences.english: The Frog-Footman repeated, in the same solemn tone, only changing the order of the words a little, “From the Queen.
sentences.korean: 개구리 하인은 똑같이 엄숙한 어조로, 다만 단어 순서만 살짝 바꿔서 “여왕 폐하께서 보내신 말씀입니다.”라고 반복했다.

sentences.english: An invitation for the Duchess to play croquet.”
sentences.korean: 공작부인을 크로케 게임에 초대합니다.

sentences.english: Then they both bowed low, and their curls got entangled together.
sentences.korean: 그러자 두 사람은 허리를 숙여 인사했고, 그들의 곱슬머리가 서로 엉켰다.

sentences.english: Alice laughed so much at this, that she had to run back into the wood for fear of their hearing her; and when she next peeped out the Fish-Footman was gone, and the other was sitting on the ground near the door, staring stupidly up into the sky.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 이 말에 너무 웃어서 그들이 들을까 봐 두려워 숲 속으로 다시 뛰어 들어가야 했습니다. 그리고 다음에 밖을 내다봤을 때는 물고기 발을 가진 남자는 사라지고 없었고, 다른 한 명은 문 근처 땅바닥에 앉아 멍하니 하늘을 바라보고 있었습니다.

sentences.english: Alice went timidly up to the door, and knocked.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 조심스럽게 문으로 다가가 노크했다.

sentences.english: “There’s no sort of use in knocking,” said the Footman, “and that for two reasons.
sentences.korean: “노크해봤자 소용없습니다.”라고 하인이 말했다. “이유는 두 가지입니다.”

sentences.english: First, because I’m on the same side of the door as you are; secondly, because they’re making such a noise inside, no one could possibly hear you.”
sentences.korean: 첫째, 제가 당신과 같은 문 쪽에 있기 때문이고, 둘째, 안에서 너무 시끄러워서 아무도 당신 말을 들을 수 없을 거예요.

sentences.english: And certainly there was a most extraordinary noise going on within—a constant howling and sneezing, and every now and then a great crash, as if a dish or kettle had been broken to pieces.
sentences.korean: 그리고 분명히 안에서는 아주 이상한 소음이 나고 있었다. 끊임없이 짖어대는 소리와 재채기 소리가 들렸고, 때때로 접시나 주전자가 산산조각 나는 듯한 큰 소리가 났다.

sentences.english: “Please, then,” said Alice, “how am I to get in?”
sentences.korean: "그럼," 앨리스가 물었다. "어떻게 들어가면 되나요?"

sentences.english: “There might be some sense in your knocking,” the Footman went on without attending to her, “if we had the door between us.
sentences.korean: 하인은 그녀를 신경 쓰지 않고 말을 이었다. "만약 우리 사이에 문이 있었다면 당신이 노크하는 데 일리가 있었을지도 모르죠."

sentences.english: For instance, if you were inside, you might knock, and I could let you out, you know.”
sentences.korean: 예를 들어, 만약 당신이 안에 있다면, 노크를 하실 수 있고, 그러면 제가 문을 열어드릴 수 있죠."

sentences.english: He was looking up into the sky all the time he was speaking, and this Alice thought decidedly uncivil.
sentences.korean: 그는 말하는 내내 하늘만 쳐다보고 있었는데, 앨리스는 그것이 상당히 무례하다고 생각했다.

sentences.english: “But perhaps he can’t help it,” she said to herself; “his eyes are so very nearly at the top of his head.
sentences.korean: "하지만 어쩌면 어쩔 수 없을지도 몰라." 그녀는 속으로 생각했다. "눈이 거의 머리 꼭대기에 붙어 있잖아."

sentences.english: But at any rate he might answer questions.—How am I to get in?”
sentences.korean: 하지만 어쨌든 그는 질문에 답해줄지도 몰라요. "어떻게 들어가면 되나요?"

sentences.english: she repeated, aloud.
sentences.korean: 그녀는 큰 소리로 반복했다.

sentences.english: “I shall sit here,” the Footman remarked, “till tomorrow—”
sentences.korean: “저는 내일까지 여기 앉아 있겠습니다.” 하인이 말했다.

sentences.english: At this moment the door of the house opened, and a large plate came skimming out, straight at the Footman’s head: it just grazed his nose, and broke to pieces against one of the trees behind him.
sentences.korean: 바로 그때 집 문이 열리더니 커다란 접시 하나가 튀어나와 하인의 머리를 향해 날아왔다. 접시는 하인의 코를 스치고 지나가더니 뒤에 있는 나무에 부딪혀 산산조각이 났다.

sentences.english: “—or next day, maybe,” the Footman continued in the same tone, exactly as if nothing had happened.
sentences.korean: "아니면 아마 다음 날쯤이겠죠." 하인은 마치 아무 일도 없었던 것처럼 똑같은 어조로 말을 이었다.

sentences.english: “How am I to get in?”
sentences.korean: "어떻게 들어가면 되나요?"

sentences.english: asked Alice again, in a louder tone.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 좀 더 큰 목소리로 다시 물었다.

sentences.english: “Are you to get in at all?”
sentences.korean: "당신은 입장할 수 있나요?"

sentences.english: said the Footman.
sentences.korean: 하인이 말했다.

sentences.english: “That’s the first question, you know.”
sentences.korean: "그게 제일 먼저 떠오르는 질문이죠."

sentences.english: It was, no doubt: only Alice did not like to be told so.
sentences.korean: 틀림없이 그랬다. 다만 앨리스는 그런 말을 듣는 것을 좋아하지 않았다.

sentences.english: “It’s really dreadful,” she muttered to herself, “the way all the creatures argue.
sentences.korean: "정말 끔찍해," 그녀는 혼잣말을 중얼거렸다. "온갖 생물들이 다투는 모습이 말이야."

sentences.english: It’s enough to drive one crazy!”
sentences.korean: 정말 미칠 지경이야!

sentences.english: The Footman seemed to think this a good opportunity for repeating his remark, with variations.
sentences.korean: 하인은 이것을 자신의 말을 약간 변형해서 반복할 좋은 기회라고 생각하는 듯했다.

sentences.english: “I shall sit here,” he said, “on and off, for days and days.”
sentences.korean: 그는 “나는 며칠이고 계속 여기 앉아 있을 것이다”라고 말했다.

sentences.english: “But what am I to do?”
sentences.korean: “하지만 저는 어떻게 해야 하죠?”

sentences.english: said Alice.
sentences.korean: 앨리스가 말했다.

sentences.english: “Anything you like,” said the Footman, and began whistling.
sentences.korean: “원하시는 건 뭐든지 말씀하세요.” 하인이 말하며 휘파람을 불기 시작했다.

sentences.english: “Oh, there’s no use in talking to him,” said Alice desperately: “he’s perfectly idiotic!”
sentences.korean: "아, 그 사람이랑 얘기해 봤자 소용없어." 앨리스가 절망적으로 말했다. "그 사람은 완전 바보야!"

sentences.english: And she opened the door and went in.
sentences.korean: 그녀는 문을 열고 안으로 들어갔다.

sentences.english: The door led right into a large kitchen, which was full of smoke from one end to the other: the Duchess was sitting on a three-legged stool in the middle, nursing a baby; the cook was leaning over the fire, stirring a large cauldron which seemed to be full of soup.
sentences.korean: 문을 열고 들어가면 바로 넓은 부엌이 나왔는데, 부엌은 한쪽 끝에서 다른 쪽 끝까지 연기로 가득 차 있었다. 공작부인은 가운데 있는 세발자전거에 앉아 아기에게 젖을 먹이고 있었고, 요리사는 불 위로 몸을 숙여 수프가 가득 담긴 듯한 커다란 가마솥을 휘젓고 있었다.

sentences.english: “There’s certainly too much pepper in that soup!”
sentences.korean: "그 수프에는 후추가 너무 많이 들어갔어!"

sentences.english: Alice said to herself, as well as she could for sneezing.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 재채기치고는 최대한 잘했다고 혼잣말을 했다.

sentences.english: There was certainly too much of it in the air.
sentences.korean: 공기 중에 그 물질이 너무 많았던 건 확실해요.

sentences.english: Even the Duchess sneezed occasionally; and as for the baby, it was sneezing and howling alternately without a moment’s pause.
sentences.korean: 심지어 공작부인도 가끔 재채기를 했고, 아기는 쉴 새 없이 재채기와 울음을 번갈아 했다.

sentences.english: The only things in the kitchen that did not sneeze, were the cook, and a large cat which was sitting on the hearth and grinning from ear to ear.
sentences.korean: 부엌에서 재채기를 하지 않은 것은 요리사와 벽난로에 앉아 활짝 웃고 있는 커다란 고양이뿐이었다.

sentences.english: “Please would you tell me,” said Alice, a little timidly, for she was not quite sure whether it was good manners for her to speak first, “why your cat grins like that?”
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 자신이 먼저 말하는 것이 예의에 맞는지 확신이 서지 않아 약간 조심스럽게 물었다. "혹시 말씀해 주시겠어요? 왜 고양이가 그렇게 웃는 거죠?"

sentences.english: “It’s a Cheshire cat,” said the Duchess, “and that’s why.
sentences.korean: "체셔 고양이잖아요." 공작부인이 말했다. "바로 그 이유예요."

sentences.english: Pig!”
sentences.korean: 돼지!"

sentences.english: She said the last word with such sudden violence that Alice quite jumped; but she saw in another moment that it was addressed to the baby, and not to her, so she took courage, and went on again:—
sentences.korean: 그녀가 마지막 말을 너무 갑작스럽고 격렬하게 내뱉어서 앨리스는 깜짝 놀랐지만, 곧 그 말이 아기에게 하는 말이지 자신에게 하는 말이 아니라는 것을 깨닫고 용기를 내어 다시 말을 이어갔다.

sentences.english: “I didn’t know that Cheshire cats always grinned; in fact, I didn’t know that cats could grin.”
sentences.korean: "체셔 고양이가 항상 웃는다는 걸 몰랐어요. 사실 고양이가 웃을 수 있다는 것 자체를 몰랐죠."

sentences.english: “They all can,” said the Duchess; “and most of ’em do.”
sentences.korean: “그들 모두 할 수 있어요.” 공작부인이 말했다. “그리고 대부분 실제로 그렇게 하고 있죠.”

sentences.english: “I don’t know of any that do,” Alice said very politely, feeling quite pleased to have got into a conversation.
sentences.korean: "그런 곳은 제가 아는 한 없어요." 앨리스는 아주 공손하게 말하며, 대화를 나눌 수 있게 된 것이 꽤 기쁘다고 생각했다.

sentences.english: “You don’t know much,” said the Duchess; “and that’s a fact.”
sentences.korean: "당신은 아는 게 별로 없어요." 공작부인이 말했다. "그건 사실이에요."

sentences.english: Alice did not at all like the tone of this remark, and thought it would be as well to introduce some other subject of conversation.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 이 말투가 전혀 마음에 들지 않아 다른 화제로 바꾸는 게 좋겠다고 생각했다.

sentences.english: While she was trying to fix on one, the cook took the cauldron of soup off the fire, and at once set to work throwing everything within her reach at the Duchess and the baby—the fire-irons came first; then followed a shower of saucepans, plates, and dishes.
sentences.korean: 그녀가 어떤 것에 집중하려고 애쓰는 동안, 요리사는 수프 솥을 불에서 내려놓고는 곧바로 손이 닿는 모든 것을 공작부인과 아기에게 던지기 시작했다. 불쏘시개가 먼저 날아왔고, 그 뒤를 이어 냄비, 접시, 그릇들이 쏟아졌다.

sentences.english: The Duchess took no notice of them even when they hit her; and the baby was howling so much already, that it was quite impossible to say whether the blows hurt it or not.
sentences.korean: 공작부인은 그들이 때려도 전혀 신경 쓰지 않았고, 아기는 이미 너무 심하게 울고 있어서 그 매질이 아기에게 아팠는지 아닌지 분간할 수 없었다.

sentences.english: “Oh, please mind what you’re doing!”
sentences.korean: “아, 제발 지금 뭘 하고 있는지 좀 조심하세요!”

sentences.english: cried Alice, jumping up and down in an agony of terror.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 극심한 공포에 질려 펄쩍펄쩍 뛰며 소리쳤다.

sentences.english: “Oh, there goes his precious nose!”
sentences.korean: "어머, 저 소중한 코가 날아갔네!"

sentences.english: as an unusually large saucepan flew close by it, and very nearly carried it off.
sentences.korean: 유난히 큰 냄비 하나가 바로 그 옆으로 날아와 하마터면 그것을 날려버릴 뻔했다.

sentences.english: “If everybody minded their own business,” the Duchess said in a hoarse growl, “the world would go round a deal faster than it does.”
sentences.korean: "모두가 자기 일에만 신경 쓴다면," 공작부인이 쉰 목소리로 으르렁거렸다. "세상은 지금보다 훨씬 빨리 돌아갈 거야."

sentences.english: “Which would not be an advantage,” said Alice, who felt very glad to get an opportunity of showing off a little of her knowledge.
sentences.korean: "그건 전혀 이점이 되지 않을 거예요." 앨리스는 이렇게 말하며 자신이 가진 지식을 조금이나마 뽐낼 기회를 얻게 되어 매우 기뻤다.

sentences.english: “Just think of what work it would make with the day and night!
sentences.korean: "낮과 밤에 걸쳐 얼마나 많은 일이 벌어질지 생각해 보세요!"

sentences.english: You see the earth takes twenty-four hours to turn round on its axis—”
sentences.korean: 아시다시피 지구는 자전축을 중심으로 한 바퀴 도는 데 24시간이 걸립니다.

sentences.english: “Talking of axes,” said the Duchess, “chop off her head!”
sentences.korean: “도끼 얘기가 나왔으니 말인데,” 공작부인이 말했다. “저 여자의 목을 베어버려!”

sentences.english: Alice glanced rather anxiously at the cook, to see if she meant to take the hint; but the cook was busily stirring the soup, and seemed not to be listening, so she went on again: “Twenty-four hours, I think; or is it twelve?
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 요리사가 눈치를 채었는지 확인하려고 다소 불안한 눈빛으로 그녀를 쳐다보았지만, 요리사는 수프를 열심히 휘젓고 있어서 듣지 못하는 것 같았다. 그래서 앨리스는 다시 말을 이었다. "24시간인 것 같은데, 아니면 12시간인가?"

sentences.english: “Oh, don’t bother me,” said the Duchess; “I never could abide figures!”
sentences.korean: “오, 귀찮게 하지 마세요.” 공작부인이 말했다. “저는 숫자 따위를 정말 싫어해요!”

sentences.english: And with that she began nursing her child again, singing a sort of lullaby to it as she did so, and giving it a violent shake at the end of every line:
sentences.korean: 그렇게 그녀는 다시 아이에게 젖을 먹이기 시작했고, 자장가 같은 노래를 불러주면서 매 소절 끝마다 아이를 세게 흔들었다.

sentences.english: “Speak roughly to your little boy, And beat him when he sneezes: He only does it to annoy, Because he knows it teases.”
sentences.korean: "아들에게 거칠게 말하고, 재채기할 때 때려도 괜찮아. 걔는 그저 약 올리려고 그러는 거야. 놀림받는 걸 아니까."

sentences.english: CHORUS.
sentences.korean: 합창.

sentences.english: (In which the cook and the baby joined):
sentences.korean: (요리사와 아기가 합류한 장면)

sentences.english: “Wow!
sentences.korean: "우와!

sentences.english: wow!
sentences.korean: 우와!

sentences.english: wow!”
sentences.korean: 우와!"

sentences.english: While the Duchess sang the second verse of the song, she kept tossing the baby violently up and down, and the poor little thing howled so, that Alice could hardly hear the words:—
sentences.korean: 공작부인이 노래 2절을 부르는 동안 아기를 격렬하게 위아래로 흔들어댔고, 불쌍한 아기는 너무 심하게 울어서 앨리스는 가사를 거의 들을 수 없었다.

sentences.english: “I speak severely to my boy, I beat him when he sneezes; For he can thoroughly enjoy The pepper when he pleases!”
sentences.korean: "나는 아들에게 엄하게 말하고, 재채기하면 때리기도 한다. 하지만 아들은 원할 때면 언제든 후추를 마음껏 즐길 수 있다!"

sentences.english: CHORUS.
sentences.korean: 합창.

sentences.english: “Wow!
sentences.korean: "우와!

sentences.english: wow!
sentences.korean: 우와!

sentences.english: wow!”
sentences.korean: 우와!"

sentences.english: “Here!
sentences.korean: "여기!

sentences.english: you may nurse it a bit, if you like!”
sentences.korean: 원하시면 조금 더 보살펴 주셔도 괜찮아요!

sentences.english: the Duchess said to Alice, flinging the baby at her as she spoke.
sentences.korean: 공작부인은 앨리스에게 말하면서 아기를 던졌다.

sentences.english: “I must go and get ready to play croquet with the Queen,” and she hurried out of the room.
sentences.korean: “여왕님과 크로케를 칠 준비를 해야 해요.” 그녀는 서둘러 방을 나섰다.

sentences.english: The cook threw a frying-pan after her as she went out, but it just missed her.
sentences.korean: 요리사는 그녀가 나가는 순간 프라이팬을 던졌지만, 아슬아슬하게 빗나갔다.

sentences.english: Alice caught the baby with some difficulty, as it was a queer-shaped little creature, and held out its arms and legs in all directions, “just like a star-fish,” thought Alice.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 아기를 잡는 데 약간 어려움을 겪었다. 아기는 생김새가 기묘했고, 팔다리를 사방으로 뻗고 있었는데, 앨리스는 "마치 불가사리 같아"라고 생각했다.

sentences.english: The poor little thing was snorting like a steam-engine when she caught it, and kept doubling itself up and straightening itself out again, so that altogether, for the first minute or two, it was as much as she could do to hold it.
sentences.korean: 그 불쌍한 작은 녀석은 그녀가 그것을 잡았을 때 증기 기관차처럼 킁킁거리며 몸을 웅크렸다가 다시 펴는 것을 반복해서, 처음 1~2분 동안은 그녀가 그것을 참는 것조차 버거울 정도였다.

sentences.english: As soon as she had made out the proper way of nursing it, (which was to twist it up into a sort of knot, and then keep tight hold of its right ear and left foot, so as to prevent its undoing itself,) she carried it out into the open air.
sentences.korean: 그녀는 그것을 제대로 돌보는 방법(그것은 그것을 일종의 매듭처럼 돌돌 말아 오른쪽 귀와 왼쪽 발을 꽉 잡고 풀리지 않도록 하는 것이었다)을 알아내자마자 그것을 데리고 밖으로 나갔다.

sentences.english: “If I don’t take this child away with me,” thought Alice, “they’re sure to kill it in a day or two: wouldn’t it be murder to leave it behind?”
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 '내가 이 아이를 데려가지 않으면, 하루 이틀 안에 분명히 죽일 거야. 아이를 두고 가는 건 살인이나 다름없잖아?'라고 생각했다.

sentences.english: She said the last words out loud, and the little thing grunted in reply (it had left off sneezing by this time).
sentences.korean: 그녀가 마지막 말을 큰 소리로 하자, 그 작은 녀석이 끙 소리를 내며 대답했다 (이때쯤엔 재채기는 멈춘 상태였다).

sentences.english: “Don’t grunt,” said Alice; “that’s not at all a proper way of expressing yourself.”
sentences.korean: “끙끙거리지 마.” 앨리스가 말했다. “그건 자기 생각을 표현하는 올바른 방법이 아니야.”

sentences.english: The baby grunted again, and Alice looked very anxiously into its face to see what was the matter with it.
sentences.korean: 아기가 다시 끙 소리를 내자 앨리스는 무슨 일인지 알아보려고 매우 불안한 ​​표정으로 아기의 얼굴을 들여다보았다.

sentences.english: There could be no doubt that it had a very turn-up nose, much more like a snout than a real nose; also its eyes were getting extremely small for a baby: altogether Alice did not like the look of the thing at all.
sentences.korean: 코가 너무 위로 솟아올라 진짜 코라기보다는 주둥이에 가까웠다는 것은 의심의 여지가 없었다. 게다가 눈은 아기치고는 너무 작았다. 앨리스는 그 녀석의 모습이 전혀 마음에 들지 않았다.

sentences.english: “But perhaps it was only sobbing,” she thought, and looked into its eyes again, to see if there were any tears.
sentences.korean: "하지만 어쩌면 그저 흐느낌이었을지도 몰라." 그녀는 생각하며 혹시 눈물이 있는지 확인하려고 다시 한번 그것의 눈을 들여다보았다.

sentences.english: No, there were no tears.
sentences.korean: 아니요, 눈물은 없었어요.

sentences.english: “If you’re going to turn into a pig, my dear,” said Alice, seriously, “I’ll have nothing more to do with you.
sentences.korean: "만약 네가 돼지로 변한다면," 앨리스가 진지하게 말했다. "난 너랑 더 이상 아무런 관계도 맺고 싶지 않아."

sentences.english: Mind now!”
sentences.korean: 지금 당장 명심하세요!

sentences.english: The poor little thing sobbed again (or grunted, it was impossible to say which), and they went on for some while in silence.
sentences.korean: 불쌍한 꼬맹이는 다시 흐느꼈다(아니면 끙끙거렸을지도 모른다. 어느 쪽인지 알 수 없었다). 그리고 그들은 한동안 침묵을 지켰다.

sentences.english: Alice was just beginning to think to herself, “Now, what am I to do with this creature when I get it home?”
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 속으로 "이 녀석을 집에 데려가면 어떻게 해야 하지?"라고 생각하기 시작했다.

sentences.english: when it grunted again, so violently, that she looked down into its face in some alarm.
sentences.korean: 그러자 그것이 다시 한번 격렬하게 으르렁거렸고, 그녀는 놀라서 그것의 얼굴을 내려다보았다.

sentences.english: This time there could be no mistake about it: it was neither more nor less than a pig, and she felt that it would be quite absurd for her to carry it further.
sentences.korean: 이번에는 틀림없었다. 그것은 그저 돼지일 뿐이었고, 그녀는 그것을 더 이상 끌고 가는 것은 매우 어리석은 짓이라고 생각했다.

sentences.english: So she set the little creature down, and felt quite relieved to see it trot away quietly into the wood.
sentences.korean: 그래서 그녀는 그 작은 생물을 내려놓았고, 그것이 조용히 숲 속으로 총총걸음으로 사라지는 것을 보고 안도감을 느꼈습니다.

sentences.english: “If it had grown up,” she said to herself, “it would have made a dreadfully ugly child: but it makes rather a handsome pig, I think.”
sentences.korean: "만약 저게 자랐다면," 그녀는 혼잣말을 했다. "끔찍하게 못생긴 아이가 됐을 텐데. 하지만 꽤 잘생긴 돼지인 것 같군."

sentences.english: And she began thinking over other children she knew, who might do very well as pigs, and was just saying to herself, “if one only knew the right way to change them—” when she was a little startled by seeing the Cheshire Cat sitting on a bough of a tree a few yards off.
sentences.korean: 그녀는 돼지로 변신하면 아주 잘 어울릴 만한 다른 아이들을 떠올리며 "어떻게 변신시켜야 할지만 알면 좋을 텐데..."라고 혼잣말을 하고 있었는데, 그때 몇 미터 떨어진 나무 가지에 체셔 고양이가 앉아 있는 것을 보고 깜짝 놀랐다.

sentences.english: The Cat only grinned when it saw Alice.
sentences.korean: 고양이는 앨리스를 보자 씩 웃기만 했다.

sentences.english: It looked good-natured, she thought: still it had very long claws and a great many teeth, so she felt that it ought to be treated with respect.
sentences.korean: 그녀는 그 동물이 온순해 보인다고 생각했지만, 발톱이 매우 길고 이빨도 많아서 존중하는 마음으로 대해야겠다고 생각했다.

sentences.english: “Cheshire Puss,” she began, rather timidly, as she did not at all know whether it would like the name: however, it only grinned a little wider.
sentences.korean: "체셔 고양이," 그녀는 고양이가 그 이름을 좋아할지 전혀 몰라서 다소 조심스럽게 말을 꺼냈다. 하지만 고양이는 오히려 더 활짝 웃었다.

sentences.english: “Come, it’s pleased so far,” thought Alice, and she went on.
sentences.korean: "좋아, 지금까지는 괜찮잖아." 앨리스는 생각하며 계속 나아갔다.

sentences.english: “Would you tell me, please, which way I ought to go from here?”
sentences.korean: “여기서 어느 길로 가야 할지 알려주시겠어요?”

sentences.english: “That depends a good deal on where you want to get to,” said the Cat.
sentences.korean: "어디로 가고 싶은지에 따라 다르죠."라고 고양이가 말했다.

sentences.english: “I don’t much care where—” said Alice.
sentences.korean: “어디든 상관없어요…”라고 앨리스가 말했다.

sentences.english: “Then it doesn’t matter which way you go,” said the Cat.
sentences.korean: "그럼 어느 길로 가든 상관없어." 고양이가 말했다.

sentences.english: “—so long as I get somewhere,” Alice added as an explanation.
sentences.korean: "어딘가에 도착하기만 하면 돼요." 앨리스가 설명을 덧붙였다.

sentences.english: “Oh, you’re sure to do that,” said the Cat, “if you only walk long enough.”
sentences.korean: "오, 분명히 그렇게 될 거야." 고양이가 말했다. "충분히 오래 걷기만 하면 말이지."

sentences.english: Alice felt that this could not be denied, so she tried another question.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 이 사실을 부인할 수 없다고 생각하여 다른 질문을 던져보았다.

sentences.english: “What sort of people live about here?”
sentences.korean: 이 근처에는 어떤 사람들이 살고 있을까요?

sentences.english: “In that direction,” the Cat said, waving its right paw round, “lives a Hatter: and in that direction,” waving the other paw, “lives a March Hare.
sentences.korean: 고양이는 오른발을 휘두르며 “저쪽 방향에는 모자 장수가 살고, 저쪽 방향에는,” 왼발을 휘두르며 “3월 토끼가 산다.”라고 말했다.

sentences.english: Visit either you like: they’re both mad.”
sentences.korean: 어느 쪽이든 가보세요. 둘 다 제정신이 아니니까요.

sentences.english: “But I don’t want to go among mad people,” Alice remarked.
sentences.korean: “하지만 저는 미친 사람들 사이에 들어가고 싶지 않아요.” 앨리스가 말했다.

sentences.english: “Oh, you can’t help that,” said the Cat: “we’re all mad here.
sentences.korean: "어쩔 수 없지." 고양이가 말했다. "우린 다 미쳤어."

sentences.english: I’m mad.
sentences.korean: 난 미쳤어.

sentences.english: You’re mad.”
sentences.korean: 너 미쳤어.

sentences.english: “How do you know I’m mad?”
sentences.korean: “내가 미쳤다는 걸 어떻게 알아요?”

sentences.english: said Alice.
sentences.korean: 앨리스가 말했다.

sentences.english: “You must be,” said the Cat, “or you wouldn’t have come here.”
sentences.korean: "그렇지 않으면 여기 오지 않았겠지." 고양이가 말했다.

sentences.english: Alice didn’t think that proved it at all; however, she went on “And how do you know that you’re mad?”
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 그것이 전혀 증명한다고 생각하지 않았지만, "그럼 당신은 자신이 미쳤다는 걸 어떻게 알아요?"라고 말을 이었다.

sentences.english: “To begin with,” said the Cat, “a dog’s not mad.
sentences.korean: 고양이가 말했다. "우선, 개는 미치지 않았어."

sentences.english: You grant that?”
sentences.korean: 당신은 그 점을 인정하는 겁니까?

sentences.english: “I suppose so,” said Alice.
sentences.korean: “그런 것 같네요.” 앨리스가 말했다.

sentences.english: “Well, then,” the Cat went on, “you see, a dog growls when it’s angry, and wags its tail when it’s pleased.
sentences.korean: "음," 고양이가 말을 이었다. "있잖아, 개는 화가 나면 으르렁거리고, 기분이 좋으면 꼬리를 흔든단다."

sentences.english: Now I growl when I’m pleased, and wag my tail when I’m angry.
sentences.korean: 이제 나는 기분이 좋으면 으르렁거리고, 화가 나면 꼬리를 흔든다.

sentences.english: Therefore I’m mad.”
sentences.korean: 그러므로 나는 미쳤다.

sentences.english: “I call it purring, not growling,” said Alice.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 "으르렁거리는 게 아니라 가르랑거리는 소리라고 불러요."라고 말했다.

sentences.english: “Call it what you like,” said the Cat.
sentences.korean: "네 마음대로 불러도 좋아." 고양이가 말했다.

sentences.english: “Do you play croquet with the Queen to-day?”
sentences.korean: "오늘 여왕님과 크로케를 치시나요?"

sentences.english: “I should like it very much,” said Alice, “but I haven’t been invited yet.”
sentences.korean: "정말 마음에 들 것 같아요." 앨리스가 말했다. "하지만 아직 초대받지 못했어요."

sentences.english: “You’ll see me there,” said the Cat, and vanished.
sentences.korean: "거기서 날 보게 될 거야." 고양이가 말하고는 사라졌다.

sentences.english: Alice was not much surprised at this, she was getting so used to queer things happening.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 이런 일에 그다지 놀라지 않았다. 이상한 일들이 일어나는 것에 이미 익숙해져 있었기 때문이다.

sentences.english: While she was looking at the place where it had been, it suddenly appeared again.
sentences.korean: 그녀가 그것이 있던 자리를 바라보고 있을 때, 그것이 갑자기 다시 나타났다.

sentences.english: “By-the-bye, what became of the baby?”
sentences.korean: 그런데 아기는 어떻게 됐어?

sentences.english: said the Cat.
sentences.korean: 고양이가 말했다.

sentences.english: “I’d nearly forgotten to ask.”
sentences.korean: “묻는 걸 깜빡할 뻔했어요.”

sentences.english: “It turned into a pig,” Alice quietly said, just as if it had come back in a natural way.
sentences.korean: "돼지로 변했어." 앨리스는 마치 자연스러운 현상인 양 조용히 말했다.

sentences.english: “I thought it would,” said the Cat, and vanished again.
sentences.korean: "그럴 줄 알았어." 고양이가 말하고는 다시 사라졌다.

sentences.english: Alice waited a little, half expecting to see it again, but it did not appear, and after a minute or two she walked on in the direction in which the March Hare was said to live.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 토끼가 다시 나타날 것을 기대하며 잠시 기다렸지만, 토끼는 나타나지 않았고, 1, 2분 후 앨리스는 3월 토끼가 산다고 전해지는 방향으로 계속 걸어갔다.

sentences.english: “I’ve seen hatters before,” she said to herself; “the March Hare will be much the most interesting, and perhaps as this is May it won’t be raving mad—at least not so mad as it was in March.”
sentences.korean: "전에도 모자 장수들을 본 적이 있어." 그녀는 혼잣말을 했다. "3월 토끼가 가장 흥미로울 거야. 게다가 지금은 5월이니까, 적어도 3월만큼 미쳐 날뛰지는 않겠지."

sentences.english: As she said this, she looked up, and there was the Cat again, sitting on a branch of a tree.
sentences.korean: 그녀가 이렇게 말하며 고개를 들자, 고양이가 다시 나무 가지에 앉아 있었다.

sentences.english: “Did you say pig, or fig?”
sentences.korean: “돼지라고 하셨어요, 아니면 무화과라고 하셨어요?”

sentences.english: said the Cat.
sentences.korean: 고양이가 말했다.

sentences.english: “I said pig,” replied Alice; “and I wish you wouldn’t keep appearing and vanishing so suddenly: you make one quite giddy.”
sentences.korean: "돼지라고 했잖아." 앨리스가 대답했다. "그리고 네가 그렇게 갑자기 나타났다 사라지지 않았으면 좋겠어. 너 때문에 어지러워 죽겠어."

sentences.english: “All right,” said the Cat; and this time it vanished quite slowly, beginning with the end of the tail, and ending with the grin, which remained some time after the rest of it had gone.
sentences.korean: "좋아." 고양이가 말했고, 이번에는 꼬리 끝부터 천천히 사라지기 시작해서, 나머지 부분이 다 사라진 후에도 한동안 남아 있던 미소까지 완전히 사라졌다.

sentences.english: “Well!
I’ve often seen a cat without a grin,” thought Alice; “but a grin without a cat!
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 "웃지 않는 고양이는 자주 봤지만, 고양이 없는 웃는 얼굴은 처음 봐!"라고 생각했다.

sentences.english: It’s the most curious thing I ever saw in my life!”
sentences.korean: 내 평생 본 것 중에 가장 신기한 일이야!

sentences.english: She had not gone much farther before she came in sight of the house of the March Hare: she thought it must be the right house, because the chimneys were shaped like ears and the roof was thatched with fur.
sentences.korean: 그녀는 얼마 가지 않아 3월 토끼의 집이 눈앞에 나타났다. 굴뚝이 귀 모양이고 지붕이 털로 덮여 있었으니, 틀림없이 그 집일 거라고 생각했다.

sentences.english: It was so large a house, that she did not like to go nearer till she had nibbled some more of the lefthand bit of mushroom, and raised herself to about two feet high: even then she walked up towards it rather timidly, saying to herself “Suppose it should be raving mad after all!
sentences.korean: 그 집은 너무 커서, 그녀는 왼쪽 버섯 조각을 좀 더 뜯어 먹고 키를 60cm 정도까지 키울 때까지는 가까이 다가가고 싶지 않았다. 그러고 나서도 그녀는 다소 겁먹은 듯 그쪽으로 걸어가며 속으로 "만약 저 집이 정말 미쳤다면 어쩌지!"라고 말했다.

sentences.english: I almost wish I’d gone to see the Hatter instead!”
sentences.korean: 차라리 모자장수 공연을 보러 갔으면 좋았을 걸 하는 생각이 드네요!

sentences.english: There was a table set out under a tree in front of the house, and the March Hare and the Hatter were having tea at it: a Dormouse was sitting between them, fast asleep, and the other two were using it as a cushion, resting their elbows on it, and talking over its head.
sentences.korean: 집 앞 나무 아래에 탁자가 차려져 있었고, 3월 토끼와 모자 장수가 그 위에서 차를 마시고 있었다. 겨울잠쥐 한 마리가 그들 사이에 곤히 잠들어 있었는데, 나머지 둘은 그 겨울잠쥐를 쿠션 삼아 팔꿈치를 얹고 머리 위로 이야기를 나누고 있었다.

sentences.english: “Very uncomfortable for the Dormouse,” thought Alice; “only, as it’s asleep, I suppose it doesn’t mind.”
sentences.korean: "겨울잠쥐에게는 아주 불편하겠군." 앨리스는 생각했다. "하지만 자고 있으니 괜찮겠지."

sentences.english: The table was a large one, but the three were all crowded together at one corner of it: “No room!
sentences.korean: 테이블은 컸지만, 세 사람은 테이블 한쪽 구석에 옹기종기 모여 앉아 있었다. "자리가 없어!"

sentences.english: No room!”
sentences.korean: 자리가 없어요!

sentences.english: they cried out when they saw Alice coming.
sentences.korean: 앨리스가 오는 것을 보자 그들은 소리쳤다.

sentences.english: “There’s plenty of room!”
sentences.korean: "공간은 충분히 있어요!"

sentences.english: said Alice indignantly, and she sat down in a large arm-chair at one end of the table.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 분개하며 말했고, 테이블 한쪽 끝에 있는 커다란 안락의자에 털썩 주저앉았다.

sentences.english: “Have some wine,” the March Hare said in an encouraging tone.
sentences.korean: "와인 좀 마셔 봐," 3월 토끼가 격려하는 어조로 말했다.

sentences.english: Alice looked all round the table, but there was nothing on it but tea.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 탁자 주위를 둘러보았지만, 탁자 위에는 차 외에는 아무것도 없었다.

sentences.english: “I don’t see any wine,” she remarked.
sentences.korean: "와인이 안 보이네요."라고 그녀가 말했다.

sentences.english: “There isn’t any,” said the March Hare.
sentences.korean: “없어요.” 3월 토끼가 말했다.

sentences.english: “Then it wasn’t very civil of you to offer it,” said Alice angrily.
sentences.korean: "그럼 그걸 제안한 건 예의 없는 행동이었네요." 앨리스가 화난 목소리로 말했다.

sentences.english: “It wasn’t very civil of you to sit down without being invited,” said the March Hare.
sentences.korean: "초대도 없이 앉은 건 예의에 어긋나는 행동이었어요."라고 3월 토끼가 말했다.

sentences.english: “I didn’t know it was your table,” said Alice; “it’s laid for a great many more than three.”
sentences.korean: "저 테이블이 당신 테이블인 줄 몰랐어요." 앨리스가 말했다. "세 명보다 훨씬 많은 사람을 위한 테이블처럼 차려져 있네요."

sentences.english: “Your hair wants cutting,” said the Hatter.
sentences.korean: 모자장수는 "머리를 잘라야겠군요."라고 말했다.

sentences.english: He had been looking at Alice for some time with great curiosity, and this was his first speech.
sentences.korean: 그는 한동안 앨리스를 호기심 어린 눈으로 바라보고 있었고, 이것이 그의 첫 번째 말이었다.

sentences.english: “You should learn not to make personal remarks,” Alice said with some severity; “it’s very rude.”
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 다소 단호한 어조로 "인신공격은 하지 않는 법을 배워야 해. 아주 무례한 행동이야."라고 말했다.

sentences.english: The Hatter opened his eyes very wide on hearing this; but all he said was, “Why is a raven like a writing-desk?”
sentences.korean: 모자장수는 이 말을 듣고 눈을 크게 떴지만, "까마귀는 왜 책상과 ​​같을까요?"라고만 말했다.

sentences.english: “Come, we shall have some fun now!”
sentences.korean: “자, 이제 신나게 놀아보자!”

sentences.english: thought Alice.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 생각했다.

sentences.english: “I’m glad they’ve begun asking riddles.—I believe I can guess that,” she added aloud.
sentences.korean: "수수께끼를 내기 시작해서 기뻐요. 제가 맞힐 수 있을 것 같아요." 그녀는 큰 소리로 덧붙였다.

sentences.english: “Do you mean that you think you can find out the answer to it?”
sentences.korean: "당신은 그 질문에 대한 답을 알아낼 수 있다고 생각하는 건가요?"

sentences.english: said the March Hare.
sentences.korean: 3월 토끼가 말했다.

sentences.english: “Exactly so,” said Alice.
sentences.korean: “정확히 그래요.” 앨리스가 말했다.

sentences.english: “Then you should say what you mean,” the March Hare went on.
sentences.korean: “그럼 네 속마음을 말해 봐.” 3월 토끼가 말을 이었다.

sentences.english: “I do,” Alice hastily replied; “at least—at least I mean what I say—that’s the same thing, you know.”
sentences.korean: "그래요," 앨리스가 황급히 대답했다. "적어도, 적어도 저는 제가 하는 말을 진심으로 하니까요. 그건 똑같은 거잖아요."

sentences.english: “Not the same thing a bit!”
sentences.korean: “전혀 다른 거예요!”

sentences.english: said the Hatter.
sentences.korean: 모자장수가 말했다.

sentences.english: “You might just as well say that ‘I see what I eat’ is the same thing as ‘I eat what I see’!”
sentences.korean: “‘나는 내가 먹는 것을 본다’라는 말은 ‘나는 내가 보는 것을 먹는다’라는 말과 같은 의미라고 할 수 있겠죠!”

sentences.english: “You might just as well say,” added the March Hare, “that ‘I like what I get’ is the same thing as ‘I get what I like’!”
sentences.korean: "마치 '나는 내가 얻는 것에 만족한다'는 말과 '나는 내가 좋아하는 것을 얻는다'는 말이 같은 뜻인 것 같군." 3월 토끼가 덧붙였다.

sentences.english: “You might just as well say,” added the Dormouse, who seemed to be talking in his sleep, “that ‘I breathe when I sleep’ is the same thing as ‘I sleep when I breathe’!”
sentences.korean: 잠꼬대를 하는 듯한 겨울잠쥐가 덧붙였다. "마치 '나는 잠을 잘 때 숨을 쉰다'는 말과 '나는 숨을 쉴 때 잠을 잔다'는 말이 똑같다고 할 수 있겠네요!"

sentences.english: “It is the same thing with you,” said the Hatter, and here the conversation dropped, and the party sat silent for a minute, while Alice thought over all she could remember about ravens and writing-desks, which wasn’t much.
sentences.korean: "너도 마찬가지야." 모자장수가 말하자 대화는 멈췄고, 일행은 잠시 침묵에 잠겼다. 앨리스는 까마귀와 책상에 대해 기억나는 모든 것을 떠올려 보았지만, 기억나는 것은 별로 없었다.

sentences.english: The Hatter was the first to break the silence.
sentences.korean: 모자장수가 먼저 침묵을 깼다.

sentences.english: “What day of the month is it?”
sentences.korean: "오늘은 무슨 요일이죠?"

sentences.english: he said, turning to Alice: he had taken his watch out of his pocket, and was looking at it uneasily, shaking it every now and then, and holding it to his ear.
sentences.korean: 그는 앨리스를 향해 몸을 돌리며 말했다. 그는 주머니에서 시계를 꺼내 불안한 듯 바라보며, 때때로 시계를 흔들고 귀에 대보았다.

sentences.english: Alice considered a little, and then said “The fourth.”
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 잠시 생각하더니 “네 번째요.”라고 말했다.

sentences.english: “Two days wrong!”
sentences.korean: "이틀이나 틀렸어요!"

sentences.english: sighed the Hatter.
sentences.korean: 모자장수는 한숨을 쉬었다.

sentences.english: “I told you butter wouldn’t suit the works!”
sentences.korean: "내가 버터는 요리에 안 어울린다고 했잖아!"

sentences.english: he added looking angrily at the March Hare.
sentences.korean: 그는 3월 토끼를 화난 눈으로 바라보며 덧붙였다.

sentences.english: “It was the best butter,” the March Hare meekly replied.
sentences.korean: "최고의 버터였어요." 3월 토끼가 나지막이 대답했다.

sentences.english: “Yes, but some crumbs must have got in as well,” the Hatter grumbled: “you shouldn’t have put it in with the bread-knife.”
sentences.korean: “그래, 하지만 빵 부스러기도 들어갔을 거야.” 모자장수가 투덜거렸다. “빵칼로 넣으면 안 됐지.”

sentences.english: The March Hare took the watch and looked at it gloomily: then he dipped it into his cup of tea, and looked at it again: but he could think of nothing better to say than his first remark, “It was the best butter, you know.”
sentences.korean: 3월 토끼는 시계를 집어 들고 침울하게 바라보았다. 그러고는 시계를 찻잔에 담갔다가 다시 바라보았지만, 처음 했던 말보다 더 나은 말이 떠오르지 않았다. "이거 진짜 좋은 버터였는데 말이야."

sentences.english: Alice had been looking over his shoulder with some curiosity.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 호기심 어린 눈으로 그의 어깨 너머로 보고 있었다.

sentences.english: “What a funny watch!”
sentences.korean: "정말 웃긴 시계네!"

sentences.english: she remarked.
sentences.korean: 그녀가 말했다.

sentences.english: “It tells the day of the month, and doesn’t tell what o’clock it is!”
sentences.korean: "그건 날짜만 알려주고, 몇 시인지는 알려주지 않아!"

sentences.english: “Why should it?”
sentences.korean: “왜 그래야 하죠?”

sentences.english: muttered the Hatter.
sentences.korean: 모자장수는 중얼거렸다.

sentences.english: “Does your watch tell you what year it is?”
sentences.korean: "당신의 시계는 지금이 몇 년도인지 알려주나요?"

sentences.english: “Of course not,” Alice replied very readily: “but that’s because it stays the same year for such a long time together.”
sentences.korean: "당연히 아니죠." 앨리스는 아주 단호하게 대답했다. "하지만 그건 그 해가 아주 오랫동안 같은 해로 유지되기 때문이에요."

sentences.english: “Which is just the case with mine,” said the Hatter.
sentences.korean: "제 경우도 마찬가지예요."라고 모자장수가 말했다.

sentences.english: Alice felt dreadfully puzzled, The Hatter’s remark seemed to have no sort of meaning in it, and yet it was certainly English.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 몹시 당황스러웠다. 모자장수의 말에는 어떤 의미도 담겨 있지 않은 것 같았지만, 분명히 영국적인 표현이었다.

sentences.english: “I don’t quite understand you,” she said, as politely as she could.
sentences.korean: "무슨 말씀인지 잘 이해가 안 돼요." 그녀는 최대한 공손하게 말했다.

sentences.english: “The Dormouse is asleep again,” said the Hatter, and he poured a little hot tea upon its nose.
sentences.korean: "겨울잠쥐가 또 잠들었군." 모자장수가 말하며 겨울잠쥐의 코에 뜨거운 차를 조금 부었다.

sentences.english: The Dormouse shook its head impatiently, and said, without opening its eyes, “Of course, of course; just what I was going to remark myself.”
sentences.korean: 겨울잠쥐는 짜증스럽게 고개를 저으며 눈을 뜨지 않고 말했다. "당연하지, 당연하지. 나도 방금 그 말을 하려고 했어."
