sentences.korean: 그들은 그 당밀을 어디서 끌어왔을까?

sentences.english: “You can draw water out of a water-well,” said the Hatter; “so I should think you could draw treacle out of a treacle-well—eh, stupid?”
sentences.korean: 모자장수는 “우물에서 물을 길어 올릴 수 있으니, 당밀 우물에서 당밀을 길어 올릴 수 있을 거라고 생각하지 않나? 바보 같으니.”라고 말했다.

sentences.english: “But they were in the well,” Alice said to the Dormouse, not choosing to notice this last remark.
sentences.korean: "하지만 걔네들은 우물 안에 있었잖아." 앨리스는 겨울잠쥐에게 말했지만, 마지막 말은 애써 못 들은 척했다.

sentences.english: “Of course they were,” said the Dormouse; “—well in.”
sentences.korean: "당연하지," 겨울잠쥐가 말했다. "—완전히 빠져 있었어."

sentences.english: This answer so confused poor Alice, that she let the Dormouse go on for some time without interrupting it.
sentences.korean: 이 대답에 너무 당황한 불쌍한 앨리스는 한동안 겨울잠쥐가 계속 이야기하도록 내버려두고 말을 끊지 않았다.

sentences.english: “They were learning to draw,” the Dormouse went on, yawning and rubbing its eyes, for it was getting very sleepy; “and they drew all manner of things—everything that begins with an M—”
sentences.korean: "걔네들은 그림 그리는 법을 배우고 있었어." 겨울잠쥐는 하품을 하고 눈을 비비며 말을 이었다. 너무 졸렸기 때문이다. "그리고 온갖 것들을 그렸지. M으로 시작하는 건 뭐든지 말이야."

sentences.english: “Why with an M?”
sentences.korean: “왜 M으로 시작하는 거죠?”

sentences.english: said Alice.
sentences.korean: 앨리스가 말했다.

sentences.english: “Why not?”
sentences.korean: "왜 안 돼?"

sentences.english: said the March Hare.
sentences.korean: 3월 토끼가 말했다.

sentences.english: Alice was silent.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 침묵했다.

sentences.english: The Dormouse had closed its eyes by this time, and was going off into a doze; but, on being pinched by the Hatter, it woke up again with a little shriek, and went on: “—that begins with an M, such as mouse-traps, and the moon, and memory, and muchness—you know you say things are “much of a muchness”—did you ever see such a thing as a drawing of a muchness?”
sentences.korean: 겨울잠쥐는 이미 눈을 감고 졸고 있었는데, 모자장수가 꼬집자 작은 비명을 지르며 다시 깨어나더니 이렇게 말했습니다. "M으로 시작하는 단어들, 예를 들어 쥐덫, 달, 기억, 그리고 '많음' 같은 것들 말이에요. '많음'이라는 표현을 쓸 때 '많은 것이 많다'라고 하잖아요. '많음'을 그림으로 표현한 걸 본 적 있어요?"

sentences.english: “Really, now you ask me,” said Alice, very much confused, “I don’t think—”
sentences.korean: "정말, 이제 와서 물어보시니," 앨리스는 몹시 당황하며 말했다. "저는 그렇게 생각하지 않는데요—"

sentences.english: “Then you shouldn’t talk,” said the Hatter.
sentences.korean: “그럼 말하지 말아야지.”라고 모자장수가 말했다.

sentences.english: This piece of rudeness was more than Alice could bear: she got up in great disgust, and walked off; the Dormouse fell asleep instantly, and neither of the others took the least notice of her going, though she looked back once or twice, half hoping that they would call after her: the last time she saw them, they were trying to put the Dormouse into the teapot.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 이 무례함을 더 이상 참을 수 없었습니다. 몹시 불쾌했던 그녀는 자리에서 일어나 걸어갔습니다. 겨울잠쥐는 곧바로 잠이 들었고, 다른 동물들은 그녀가 가는 것을 전혀 신경 쓰지 않았습니다. 앨리스는 혹시라도 그들이 자신을 불러주기를 바라며 한두 번 뒤돌아보았지만, 마지막으로 그들을 본 것은 겨울잠쥐를 찻주전자에 넣으려는 모습이었습니다.

sentences.english: “At any rate I’ll never go there again!”
sentences.korean: 어쨌든 난 다시는 그곳에 가지 않을 거야!

sentences.english: said Alice as she picked her way through the wood.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 숲 속을 헤쳐나가며 말했다.

sentences.english: “It’s the stupidest tea-party I ever was at in all my life!”
sentences.korean: "내 평생 가본 티 파티 중에 제일 멍청한 파티였어!"

sentences.english: Just as she said this, she noticed that one of the trees had a door leading right into it.
sentences.korean: 그녀가 이렇게 말하는 순간, 나무 중 하나에 바로 안으로 통하는 문이 있는 것을 발견했다.

sentences.english: “That’s very curious!”
sentences.korean: “정말 신기하네요!”

sentences.english: she thought.
sentences.korean: 그녀는 생각했다.

sentences.english: “But everything’s curious today.
sentences.korean: “하지만 오늘은 모든 게 다 신기하네요.”

sentences.english: I think I may as well go in at once.”
sentences.korean: "그냥 바로 들어가 버리는 게 좋겠어."

sentences.english: And in she went.
sentences.korean: 그리고 그녀는 안으로 들어갔다.

sentences.english: Once more she found herself in the long hall, and close to the little glass table.
sentences.korean: 그녀는 다시 긴 복도에 서서 작은 유리 탁자 가까이에 서 있는 자신을 발견했다.

sentences.english: “Now, I’ll manage better this time,” she said to herself, and began by taking the little golden key, and unlocking the door that led into the garden.
sentences.korean: "이번엔 더 잘 해낼 거야." 그녀는 혼잣말을 하며 작은 금빛 열쇠를 집어 들고 정원으로 통하는 문을 열기 시작했다.

sentences.english: Then she went to work nibbling at the mushroom (she had kept a piece of it in her pocket) till she was about a foot high: then she walked down the little passage: and then—she found herself at last in the beautiful garden, among the bright flower-beds and the cool fountains.
sentences.korean: 그녀는 주머니에 버섯 조각을 넣어두었다가 조금씩 갉아먹기 시작했고, 마침내 키가 30cm쯤 될 때까지 자라났다. 그런 다음 작은 통로를 따라 걸어갔고, 마침내 화려한 꽃밭과 시원한 분수가 있는 아름다운 정원에 도착했다.

sentences.english: A large rose-tree stood near the entrance of the garden: the roses growing on it were white, but there were three gardeners at it, busily painting them red.
sentences.korean: 정원 입구 근처에는 커다란 장미나무 한 그루가 서 있었다. 나무에 핀 장미는 하얀색이었지만, 세 명의 정원사가 분주하게 장미를 빨갛게 칠하고 있었다.

sentences.english: Alice thought this a very curious thing, and she went nearer to watch them, and just as she came up to them she heard one of them say, “Look out now, Five!
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 이것이 매우 이상한 일이라고 생각하여 그들을 더 가까이에서 지켜보았고, 바로 그때 그들 중 한 명이 "조심해, 파이브!"라고 말하는 것을 들었다.

sentences.english: Don’t go splashing paint over me like that!”
sentences.korean: 나한테 페인트를 그렇게 튀기지 마!

sentences.english: “I couldn’t help it,” said Five, in a sulky tone; “Seven jogged my elbow.”
sentences.korean: "어쩔 수 없었어." 파이브가 퉁명스럽게 말했다. "세븐이 내 팔꿈치를 툭 쳤거든."

sentences.english: On which Seven looked up and said, “That’s right, Five!
sentences.korean: 그러자 세븐이 고개를 들어 "맞아, 파이브!"라고 말했다.

sentences.english: Always lay the blame on others!”
sentences.korean: 항상 남 탓만 하세요!

sentences.english: “You’d better not talk!”
sentences.korean: “말하지 않는 게 좋을 거야!”

sentences.english: said Five.
sentences.korean: 파이브가 말했다.

sentences.english: “I heard the Queen say only yesterday you deserved to be beheaded!”
sentences.korean: "어제 여왕께서 당신은 참수당해도 마땅하다고 말씀하시는 걸 들었어요!"

sentences.english: “What for?”
sentences.korean: "무엇 때문에?"

sentences.english: said the one who had spoken first.
sentences.korean: 먼저 말했던 사람이 말했다.

sentences.english: “That’s none of your business, Two!”
sentences.korean: “그건 네가 상관할 일이 아니야, 투!”

sentences.english: said Seven.
sentences.korean: 세븐이 말했다.

sentences.english: “Yes, it is his business!”
sentences.korean: 네, 그건 그의 사업이죠!

sentences.english: said Five, “and I’ll tell him—it was for bringing the cook tulip-roots instead of onions.”
sentences.korean: 파이브가 말했다. "내가 그에게 말해줄게. 양파 대신 튤립 뿌리를 요리사에게 가져다 줬기 때문이야."

sentences.english: Seven flung down his brush, and had just begun “Well, of all the unjust things—” when his eye chanced to fall upon Alice, as she stood watching them, and he checked himself suddenly: the others looked round also, and all of them bowed low.
sentences.korean: 세븐은 붓을 내던지고 "세상에, 온갖 불공평한 일들이 다 있구나—"라고 막 말을 시작하려던 찰나, 그들을 지켜보고 있는 앨리스에게 시선이 닿자 갑자기 말을 멈췄다. 다른 사람들도 주위를 둘러보고 모두 허리를 숙여 인사했다.

sentences.english: “Would you tell me,” said Alice, a little timidly, “why you are painting those roses?”
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 약간 수줍게 “왜 장미를 그리고 계신지 말씀해 주시겠어요?”라고 물었다.

sentences.english: Five and Seven said nothing, but looked at Two.
sentences.korean: 파이브와 세븐은 아무 말도 하지 않고 투를 바라보았다.

sentences.english: Two began in a low voice, “Why the fact is, you see, Miss, this here ought to have been a red rose-tree, and we put a white one in by mistake; and if the Queen was to find it out, we should all have our heads cut off, you know.
sentences.korean: 두 사람은 낮은 목소리로 말하기 시작했다. "사실은 말이죠, 아가씨, 여기 있는 장미나무는 원래 붉은 장미나무여야 했는데, 저희가 실수로 흰 장미나무를 심었어요. 만약 여왕께서 이 사실을 아시게 되면 저희 모두 목이 잘릴 거예요."

sentences.english: So you see, Miss, we’re doing our best, afore she comes, to—” At this moment Five, who had been anxiously looking across the garden, called out “The Queen!
sentences.korean: 그러니까 아가씨, 저희는 여왕님이 오시기 전에 최선을 다하고 있는 거예요—” 바로 그때, 정원을 불안하게 바라보고 있던 파이브가 “여왕님!” 하고 외쳤다.

sentences.english: The Queen!”
sentences.korean: 여왕님!

sentences.english: and the three gardeners instantly threw themselves flat upon their faces.
sentences.korean: 그러자 세 명의 정원사는 즉시 얼굴을 땅에 대고 엎드렸다.

sentences.english: There was a sound of many footsteps, and Alice looked round, eager to see the Queen.
sentences.korean: 많은 발소리가 들렸고, 앨리스는 여왕을 보고 싶어 주위를 둘러보았다.

sentences.english: First came ten soldiers carrying clubs; these were all shaped like the three gardeners, oblong and flat, with their hands and feet at the corners: next the ten courtiers; these were ornamented all over with diamonds, and walked two and two, as the soldiers did.
sentences.korean: 먼저 곤봉을 든 열 명의 병사가 따라왔는데, 이 곤봉들은 모두 세 명의 정원사처럼 길쭉하고 납작했으며, 손과 발이 모서리에 달려 있었다. 그 다음으로는 열 명의 신하들이 따라왔는데, 이들은 온몸에 다이아몬드로 장식되어 있었고, 병사들처럼 두 명씩 짝을 지어 걸었다.

sentences.english: After these came the royal children; there were ten of them, and the little dears came jumping merrily along hand in hand, in couples: they were all ornamented with hearts.
sentences.korean: 그 뒤를 이어 왕족 아이들이 왔는데, 열 명이나 되었고, 귀여운 아이들은 손을 잡고, 짝을 지어 즐겁게 뛰어다녔습니다. 아이들 모두 하트 무늬로 장식되어 있었습니다.

sentences.english: Next came the guests, mostly Kings and Queens, and among them Alice recognised the White Rabbit: it was talking in a hurried nervous manner, smiling at everything that was said, and went by without noticing her.
sentences.korean: 다음으로 손님들이 도착했는데, 대부분 왕과 왕비들이었고, 그중 앨리스는 흰 토끼를 알아보았습니다. 흰 토끼는 초조하고 불안한 말투로 이야기하며 모든 말에 미소를 지었고, 앨리스를 알아채지 못한 채 지나갔습니다.

sentences.english: Then followed the Knave of Hearts, carrying the King’s crown on a crimson velvet cushion; and, last of all this grand procession, came THE KING AND QUEEN OF HEARTS.
sentences.korean: 그 뒤를 이어 하트의 잭이 진홍색 벨벳 쿠션 위에 왕관을 얹고 행진했고, 이 성대한 행렬의 마지막에는 하트의 왕과 여왕이 등장했습니다.

sentences.english: Alice was rather doubtful whether she ought not to lie down on her face like the three gardeners, but she could not remember ever having heard of such a rule at processions; “and besides, what would be the use of a procession,” thought she, “if people had all to lie down upon their faces, so that they couldn’t see it?”
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 자신도 세 정원사처럼 엎드려야 하는지 약간 의심스러웠지만, 행렬에서 그런 규칙이 있다는 말을 들어본 적이 없었던 것 같았다. "게다가 사람들이 모두 엎드려서 행렬을 볼 수 없다면 행렬이 무슨 소용이 있겠어?"라고 그녀는 생각했다.

sentences.english: So she stood still where she was, and waited.
sentences.korean: 그래서 그녀는 그 자리에 가만히 서서 기다렸다.

sentences.english: When the procession came opposite to Alice, they all stopped and looked at her, and the Queen said severely “Who is this?”
sentences.korean: 행렬이 앨리스 맞은편에 다다르자 모두 멈춰 서서 그녀를 바라보았고, 여왕은 엄숙하게 “이 사람은 누구냐?”라고 말했다.

sentences.english: She said it to the Knave of Hearts, who only bowed and smiled in reply.
sentences.korean: 그녀가 하트의 잭에게 그렇게 말하자, 그는 그저 고개를 숙이고 미소로 답했다.

sentences.english: “Idiot!”
sentences.korean: "바보!"

sentences.english: said the Queen, tossing her head impatiently; and, turning to Alice, she went on, “What’s your name, child?”
sentences.korean: 여왕은 조바심 나게 고개를 휙 돌리며 말했고, 앨리스에게로 돌아서서 “꼬마야, 이름이 뭐니?”라고 물었다.

sentences.english: “My name is Alice, so please your Majesty,” said Alice very politely; but she added, to herself, “Why, they’re only a pack of cards, after all.
sentences.korean: "제 이름은 앨리스입니다, 폐하." 앨리스는 아주 공손하게 말했지만, 속으로는 '어차피 카드 한 벌일 뿐이잖아.'라고 덧붙였다.

sentences.english: I needn’t be afraid of them!”
sentences.korean: 나는 그들을 두려워할 필요가 없어!

sentences.english: “And who are these?”
sentences.korean: “그럼 이들은 누구입니까?”

sentences.english: said the Queen, pointing to the three gardeners who were lying round the rose-tree; for, you see, as they were lying on their faces, and the pattern on their backs was the same as the rest of the pack, she could not tell whether they were gardeners, or soldiers, or courtiers, or three of her own children.
sentences.korean: 여왕은 장미나무 주위에 널브러져 있는 세 명의 정원사를 가리키며 말했다. "보시다시피, 그들은 모두 엎드려 있었고, 등에 있는 무늬도 다른 무리들과 똑같아서, 그들이 정원사인지, 군인인지, 신하인지, 아니면 자신의 아이들 중 세 명인지 구별할 수 없었기 때문입니다."

sentences.english: “How should I know?”
sentences.korean: “제가 어떻게 알겠어요?”

sentences.english: said Alice, surprised at her own courage.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 자신의 용기에 놀라며 말했다.

sentences.english: “It’s no business of mine.”
sentences.korean: “그건 내가 상관할 일이 아니야.”

sentences.english: The Queen turned crimson with fury, and, after glaring at her for a moment like a wild beast, screamed “Off with her head!
sentences.korean: 여왕은 분노로 얼굴이 새빨개졌고, 마치 야수처럼 잠시 그녀를 노려본 후 "저 여자의 목을 베어라!"라고 소리쳤다.

sentences.english: Off—”
sentences.korean: 끄다-"

sentences.english: “Nonsense!”
sentences.korean: "무의미한 말!"

sentences.english: said Alice, very loudly and decidedly, and the Queen was silent.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 아주 크고 단호하게 말했고, 여왕은 아무 말도 하지 않았다.

sentences.english: The King laid his hand upon her arm, and timidly said “Consider, my dear: she is only a child!”
sentences.korean: 왕은 그녀의 팔에 손을 얹고 조심스럽게 말했다. "여보, 생각해 보십시오. 그녀는 아직 어린아이일 뿐입니다!"

sentences.english: The Queen turned angrily away from him, and said to the Knave “Turn them over!”
sentences.korean: 여왕은 화가 나서 그에게서 등을 돌리고는 하인에게 “그것들을 뒤집어라!”라고 말했다.

sentences.english: The Knave did so, very carefully, with one foot.
sentences.korean: 잭은 한 발로 아주 조심스럽게 그렇게 했다.

sentences.english: “Get up!”
sentences.korean: “일어나!”

sentences.english: said the Queen, in a shrill, loud voice, and the three gardeners instantly jumped up, and began bowing to the King, the Queen, the royal children, and everybody else.
sentences.korean: 여왕이 날카롭고 큰 목소리로 말하자, 세 명의 정원사는 즉시 벌떡 일어나 왕과 왕비, 왕실 아이들, 그리고 다른 모든 사람들에게 절을 하기 시작했다.

sentences.english: “Leave off that!”
sentences.korean: "그만둬!"

sentences.english: screamed the Queen.
sentences.korean: 여왕은 비명을 질렀다.

sentences.english: “You make me giddy.”
sentences.korean: "당신 때문에 어지러워요."

sentences.english: And then, turning to the rose-tree, she went on, “What have you been doing here?”
sentences.korean: 그러고 나서 그녀는 장미나무를 향해 돌아서서 말을 이었다. "여기서 뭘 하고 있었던 거야?"

sentences.english: “May it please your Majesty,” said Two, in a very humble tone, going down on one knee as he spoke, “we were trying—”
sentences.korean: “폐하, 부디 양해해 주시길 바랍니다.” 투는 매우 겸손한 어조로 말하며 한쪽 무릎을 꿇었다. “저희는…”

sentences.english: “I see!”
sentences.korean: "알겠어요!"

sentences.english: said the Queen, who had meanwhile been examining the roses.
sentences.korean: 여왕은 그동안 장미를 자세히 살펴보고 있었다.

sentences.english: “Off with their heads!”
sentences.korean: "저놈들의 목을 베어라!"

sentences.english: and the procession moved on, three of the soldiers remaining behind to execute the unfortunate gardeners, who ran to Alice for protection.
sentences.korean: 행렬은 계속 나아갔고, 세 명의 병사만 남아서 불행한 정원사들을 처형했다. 정원사들은 앨리스에게 보호를 요청하며 도망쳤다.

sentences.english: “You shan’t be beheaded!”
sentences.korean: “너는 참수당하지 않을 것이다!”

sentences.english: said Alice, and she put them into a large flower-pot that stood near.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 그렇게 말하고는 근처에 놓여 있던 커다란 화분에 그것들을 넣었다.

sentences.english: The three soldiers wandered about for a minute or two, looking for them, and then quietly marched off after the others.
sentences.korean: 세 명의 병사는 1, 2분 정도 주변을 서성이며 그들을 찾다가 조용히 다른 사람들을 따라 걸어갔다.

sentences.english: “Are their heads off?”
sentences.korean: "그들의 머리가 잘려나간 건가요?"

sentences.english: shouted the Queen.
sentences.korean: 여왕이 소리쳤다.

sentences.english: “Their heads are gone, if it please your Majesty!”
sentences.korean: "폐하, 저들의 목은 이미 잘렸습니다!"

sentences.english: the soldiers shouted in reply.
sentences.korean: 병사들이 소리쳐 대답했다.

sentences.english: “That’s right!”
sentences.korean: "좋아요!"

sentences.english: shouted the Queen.
sentences.korean: 여왕이 소리쳤다.

sentences.english: “Can you play croquet?”
sentences.korean: “크로케 할 줄 아세요?”

sentences.english: The soldiers were silent, and looked at Alice, as the question was evidently meant for her.
sentences.korean: 군인들은 아무 말 없이 앨리스를 바라보았다. 질문이 분명히 그녀를 향한 것이었기 때문이다.

sentences.english: “Yes!”
shouted Alice.
sentences.korean: 앨리스가 소리쳤다.

sentences.english: “Come on, then!”
sentences.korean: “자, 그럼 어서 와 봐!”

sentences.english: roared the Queen, and Alice joined the procession, wondering very much what would happen next.
sentences.korean: 여왕이 고함을 지르자 앨리스는 다음에 무슨 일이 일어날지 몹시 궁금해하며 행렬에 합류했다.

sentences.english: “It’s—it’s a very fine day!”
sentences.korean: "오늘은… 오늘은 날씨가 정말 좋네요!"

sentences.english: said a timid voice at her side.
sentences.korean: 그녀 옆에서 조심스러운 목소리가 말했다.

sentences.english: She was walking by the White Rabbit, who was peeping anxiously into her face.
sentences.korean: 그녀는 하얀 토끼 옆을 걷고 있었는데, 하얀 토끼는 불안한 듯 그녀의 얼굴을 들여다보고 있었다.

sentences.english: “Very,” said Alice: “—where’s the Duchess?”
sentences.korean: “정말 그래요.” 앨리스가 말했다. “공작부인은 어디 계세요?”

sentences.english: “Hush!
Hush!”
said the Rabbit in a low, hurried tone.
sentences.korean: 토끼는 낮고 다급한 목소리로 말했다.

sentences.english: He looked anxiously over his shoulder as he spoke, and then raised himself upon tiptoe, put his mouth close to her ear, and whispered “She’s under sentence of execution.”
sentences.korean: 그는 말을 하면서 불안한 듯 어깨 너머로 주위를 살피더니, 발끝으로 서서 그녀의 귀에 입을 가까이 대고 속삭였다. "그녀는 사형 선고를 받았어."

sentences.english: “What for?”
sentences.korean: "무엇 때문에?"

sentences.english: said Alice.
sentences.korean: 앨리스가 말했다.

sentences.english: “Did you say ‘What a pity!’?”
sentences.korean: "혹시 '정말 안됐네요!'라고 하셨어요?"

sentences.english: the Rabbit asked.
sentences.korean: 토끼가 물었다.

sentences.english: “No, I didn’t,” said Alice: “I don’t think it’s at all a pity.
sentences.korean: “아니요, 그렇지 않았어요.” 앨리스가 말했다. “전 전혀 안타까운 일이라고 생각하지 않아요.”

sentences.english: I said ‘What for?’”
sentences.korean: 나는 “왜요?”라고 물었다.

sentences.english: “She boxed the Queen’s ears—” the Rabbit began.
sentences.korean: “그녀가 여왕의 귀를 때렸어요—” 토끼가 말을 시작했다.

sentences.english: Alice gave a little scream of laughter.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 작게 웃음을 터뜨렸다.

sentences.english: “Oh, hush!”
sentences.korean: “아, 조용히 해!”

sentences.english: the Rabbit whispered in a frightened tone.
sentences.korean: 토끼는 겁에 질린 목소리로 속삭였다.

sentences.english: “The Queen will hear you!
sentences.korean: 여왕께서 당신의 말씀을 들으실 것입니다!

sentences.english: You see, she came rather late, and the Queen said—”
sentences.korean: 아시다시피, 그녀는 다소 늦게 도착했고, 여왕께서 말씀하셨습니다—”

sentences.english: “Get to your places!”
sentences.korean: "어서 제자리로 가세요!"

sentences.english: shouted the Queen in a voice of thunder, and people began running about in all directions, tumbling up against each other; however, they got settled down in a minute or two, and the game began.
sentences.korean: 여왕이 천둥 같은 목소리로 외치자 사람들은 사방으로 뛰어다니며 서로 부딪혔지만, 1~2분 만에 진정되고 게임이 시작되었다.

sentences.english: Alice thought she had never seen such a curious croquet-ground in her life; it was all ridges and furrows; the balls were live hedgehogs, the mallets live flamingoes, and the soldiers had to double themselves up and to stand on their hands and feet, to make the arches.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 평생 그렇게 기묘한 크로케 경기장을 본 적이 없다고 생각했다. 경기장은 온통 이랑과 고랑으로 이루어져 있었고, 공은 살아있는 고슴도치였으며, 말렛은 살아있는 플라밍고였고, 병사들은 아치를 만들기 위해 몸을 웅크리고 손과 발로 서 있어야 했다.

sentences.english: The chief difficulty Alice found at first was in managing her flamingo: she succeeded in getting its body tucked away, comfortably enough, under her arm, with its legs hanging down, but generally, just as she had got its neck nicely straightened out, and was going to give the hedgehog a blow with its head, it would twist itself round and look up in her face, with such a puzzled expression that she could not help bursting out laughing: and when she had got its head down, and was going to begin again, it was very provoking to find that the hedgehog had unrolled itself, and was in the act of crawling away: besides all this, there was generally a ridge or furrow in the way wherever she wanted to send the hedgehog to, and, as the doubled-up soldiers were always getting up and walking off to other parts of the ground, Alice soon came to the conclusion that it was a very difficult game indeed.
sentences.korean: 앨리스가 처음 겪었던 가장 큰 어려움은 플라밍고를 다루는 것이었습니다. 플라밍고의 몸통은 팔 아래에 편안하게 끼워 넣고 다리는 아래로 늘어뜨리는 데 성공했지만, 목을 쭉 펴서 고슴도치를 머리로 쳐내려고 할 때마다 플라밍고는 몸을 비틀어 앨리스의 얼굴을 올려다보며 어리둥절한 표정을 지었고, 앨리스는 웃음을 참을 수 없었습니다. 플라밍고의 머리를 다시 내려놓고 다시 시작하려고 하면 고슴도치는 몸을 펴고 기어가는 바람에 더욱 짜증이 났습니다. 게다가 고슴도치를 보내려는 곳마다 둑이나 고랑이 있었고, 두 겹으로 웅크린 플라밍고는 자꾸만 일어나 다른 곳으로 걸어가 버렸습니다. 앨리스는 곧 이 게임이 정말 어렵다는 결론을 내렸습니다.

sentences.english: The players all played at once without waiting for turns, quarrelling all the while, and fighting for the hedgehogs; and in a very short time the Queen was in a furious passion, and went stamping about, and shouting “Off with his head!”
sentences.korean: 플레이어들은 차례를 기다리지 않고 모두 동시에 게임을 시작했고, 끊임없이 다투고 고슴도치를 차지하려고 싸웠습니다. 얼마 지나지 않아 여왕은 격노하여 발을 구르며 "저놈의 목을 베어라!"라고 소리쳤습니다.

sentences.english: or “Off with her head!”
sentences.korean: 또는 “목을 베어라!”

sentences.english: about once in a minute.
sentences.korean: 약 1분에 한 번 정도요.

sentences.english: Alice began to feel very uneasy: to be sure, she had not as yet had any dispute with the Queen, but she knew that it might happen any minute, “and then,” thought she, “what would become of me?
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 몹시 불안해지기 시작했다. 물론 아직 여왕과 다툼을 벌인 적은 없었지만, 언제든 그런 일이 일어날 수 있다는 것을 알고 있었기 때문이다. "그렇게 되면," 그녀는 생각했다. "나는 어떻게 되는 거지?"

sentences.english: They’re dreadfully fond of beheading people here; the great wonder is, that there’s any one left alive!”
sentences.korean: 이곳 사람들은 참수하는 걸 끔찍하게 좋아해. 살아남은 사람이 있다는 게 정말 신기할 따름이야!

sentences.english: She was looking about for some way of escape, and wondering whether she could get away without being seen, when she noticed a curious appearance in the air: it puzzled her very much at first, but, after watching it a minute or two, she made it out to be a grin, and she said to herself “It’s the Cheshire Cat: now I shall have somebody to talk to.”
sentences.korean: 그녀는 탈출할 방법을 찾으려고 주위를 둘러보며 아무도 보지 못하게 도망칠 수 있을지 생각하고 있었는데, 그때 허공에 이상한 형체가 나타나는 것을 발견했습니다. 처음에는 몹시 당황했지만, 1, 2분 정도 지켜보니 그것은 마치 웃는 얼굴 같았습니다. 그녀는 속으로 "체셔 고양이잖아! 이제 이야기할 상대가 생겼군."이라고 생각했습니다.

sentences.english: “How are you getting on?”
sentences.korean: "잘 지내고 있어요?"

sentences.english: said the Cat, as soon as there was mouth enough for it to speak with.
sentences.korean: 고양이는 말할 수 있을 만큼 입이 생기자마자 그렇게 말했다.

sentences.english: Alice waited till the eyes appeared, and then nodded.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 눈이 나타날 때까지 기다렸다가 고개를 끄덕였다.

sentences.english: “It’s no use speaking to it,” she thought, “till its ears have come, or at least one of them.”
sentences.korean: "귀가 나기 전까지는, 아니, 적어도 하나라도 나기 전까지는 말을 걸어봤자 소용없어." 그녀는 생각했다.

sentences.english: In another minute the whole head appeared, and then Alice put down her flamingo, and began an account of the game, feeling very glad she had someone to listen to her.
sentences.korean: 잠시 후 플라밍고 머리 전체가 나타났고, 앨리스는 플라밍고 인형을 내려놓고 게임에 대해 이야기하기 시작했습니다. 누군가 자신의 이야기를 들어준다는 사실에 매우 기뻤습니다.

sentences.english: The Cat seemed to think that there was enough of it now in sight, and no more of it appeared.
sentences.korean: 고양이는 이제 눈앞에 보이는 것이 충분하다고 생각하는 듯했고, 더 이상 그것은 나타나지 않았다.

sentences.english: “I don’t think they play at all fairly,” Alice began, in rather a complaining tone, “and they all quarrel so dreadfully one can’t hear oneself speak—and they don’t seem to have any rules in particular; at least, if there are, nobody attends to them—and you’ve no idea how confusing it is all the things being alive; for instance, there’s the arch I’ve got to go through next walking about at the other end of the ground—and I should have croqueted the Queen’s hedgehog just now, only it ran away when it saw mine coming!”
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 다소 불평하는 어조로 말을 시작했다. "제 생각에 그들은 전혀 공정하게 놀지 않아요. 다들 너무 심하게 싸워서 제 말소리도 안 들릴 정도예요. 게다가 특별한 규칙도 없는 것 같아요. 설령 규칙이 있다 하더라도 아무도 지키지 않아요. 그리고 모든 게 살아 움직이는 게 얼마나 혼란스러운지 당신은 상상도 못 할 거예요. 예를 들어, 운동장 저 끝에는 제가 지나가야 할 아치가 있고, 방금 전에 여왕님의 고슴도치를 크로켓으로 칠 뻔했는데, 제 고슴도치가 오는 걸 보고 도망가 버렸어요!"

sentences.english: “How do you like the Queen?”
sentences.korean: “여왕님은 어떠세요?”

sentences.english: said the Cat in a low voice.
sentences.korean: 고양이가 나지막한 목소리로 말했다.

sentences.english: “Not at all,” said Alice: “she’s so extremely—” Just then she noticed that the Queen was close behind her, listening: so she went on, “—likely to win, that it’s hardly worth while finishing the game.”
sentences.korean: “전혀 아니에요.” 앨리스가 말했다. “그녀는 너무나도—” 그때 앨리스는 여왕이 바로 뒤에서 듣고 있다는 것을 알아차리고는 말을 이었다. “—이길 가능성이 너무 높아서 게임을 끝까지 할 가치가 거의 없어요.”

sentences.english: The Queen smiled and passed on.
sentences.korean: 여왕은 미소를 지으며 지나갔다.

sentences.english: “Who are you talking to?”
sentences.korean: 누구랑 얘기하고 있는 거야?

sentences.english: said the King, going up to Alice, and looking at the Cat’s head with great curiosity.
sentences.korean: 왕은 앨리스에게 다가가 고양이의 머리를 호기심 가득한 눈으로 바라보며 말했다.

sentences.english: “It’s a friend of mine—a Cheshire Cat,” said Alice: “allow me to introduce it.”
sentences.korean: "제 친구예요. 체셔 고양이랍니다." 앨리스가 말했다. "소개해 드릴게요."

sentences.english: “I don’t like the look of it at all,” said the King: “however, it may kiss my hand if it likes.”
sentences.korean: “전혀 마음에 들지 않는 모양새지만, 원한다면 내 손에 입맞춰도 좋다.”라고 왕이 말했다.

sentences.english: “I’d rather not,” the Cat remarked.
sentences.korean: "그러고 싶지 않아." 고양이가 말했다.

sentences.english: “Don’t be impertinent,” said the King, “and don’t look at me like that!”
sentences.korean: “건방지게 굴지 마라.” 왕이 말했다. “그리고 그런 눈으로 나를 쳐다보지 마라!”

sentences.english: He got behind Alice as he spoke.
sentences.korean: 그는 말을 하면서 앨리스 뒤로 다가갔다.

sentences.english: “A cat may look at a king,” said Alice.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 “고양이가 왕을 쳐다볼 수도 있죠.”라고 말했다.

sentences.english: “I’ve read that in some book, but I don’t remember where.”
sentences.korean: “어떤 책에서 읽었는데, 어디였는지는 기억이 안 나요.”

sentences.english: “Well, it must be removed,” said the King very decidedly, and he called the Queen, who was passing at the moment, “My dear!
sentences.korean: “좋아, 그것은 제거해야 해.” 왕은 매우 단호하게 말하며 마침 지나가던 왕비를 불러 “여보!” 하고 불렀다.

sentences.english: I wish you would have this cat removed!”
sentences.korean: 이 고양이 좀 치워주셨으면 좋겠어요!

sentences.english: The Queen had only one way of settling all difficulties, great or small.
sentences.korean: 여왕에게는 크고 작은 모든 어려움을 해결할 수 있는 단 한 가지 방법밖에 없었다.

sentences.english: “Off with his head!”
sentences.korean: "저놈의 목을 베어라!"

sentences.english: she said, without even looking round.
sentences.korean: 그녀는 주위를 둘러보지도 않고 말했다.

sentences.english: “I’ll fetch the executioner myself,” said the King eagerly, and he hurried off.
sentences.korean: “내가 직접 사형집행인을 데려오겠다.” 왕은 열정적으로 말하며 서둘러 떠났다.

sentences.english: Alice thought she might as well go back, and see how the game was going on, as she heard the Queen’s voice in the distance, screaming with passion.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 멀리서 여왕의 격렬한 외침이 들려오는 것을 듣고, 게임이 어떻게 진행되고 있는지 보러 돌아가는 게 좋겠다고 생각했다.

sentences.english: She had already heard her sentence three of the players to be executed for having missed their turns, and she did not like the look of things at all, as the game was in such confusion that she never knew whether it was her turn or not.
sentences.korean: 그녀는 이미 차례를 놓친 세 명의 플레이어에게 사형을 선고하는 판결을 들었고, 게임이 너무 혼란스러워서 자기 차례인지 아닌지조차 알 수 없었기에 상황이 전혀 마음에 들지 않았다.

sentences.english: So she went in search of her hedgehog.
sentences.korean: 그래서 그녀는 고슴도치를 찾아 나섰다.

sentences.english: The hedgehog was engaged in a fight with another hedgehog, which seemed to Alice an excellent opportunity for croqueting one of them with the other: the only difficulty was, that her flamingo was gone across to the other side of the garden, where Alice could see it trying in a helpless sort of way to fly up into a tree.
sentences.korean: 고슴도치 한 마리가 다른 고슴도치와 싸우고 있었는데, 앨리스는 이 기회를 틈타 고슴도치 한 마리를 크로켓으로 때려눕히려고 했다. 하지만 문제는 앨리스의 플라밍고가 정원 반대편으로 가버렸다는 것이었다. 앨리스는 플라밍고가 그곳에서 나무 위로 날아오르려고 애쓰는 모습을 볼 수 있었다.

sentences.english: By the time she had caught the flamingo and brought it back, the fight was over, and both the hedgehogs were out of sight: “but it doesn’t matter much,” thought Alice, “as all the arches are gone from this side of the ground.”
sentences.korean: 앨리스가 플라밍고를 잡아서 데려왔을 때는 이미 싸움은 끝났고, 두 고슴도치는 시야에서 사라져 버렸다. "하지만 별로 상관없어." 앨리스는 생각했다. "이쪽 땅에서는 아치들이 모두 사라졌으니까."

sentences.english: So she tucked it away under her arm, that it might not escape again, and went back for a little more conversation with her friend.
sentences.korean: 그래서 그녀는 그것이 다시 도망가지 못하도록 팔 아래에 꼭 끼우고 친구와 좀 더 이야기를 나누러 돌아갔다.

sentences.english: When she got back to the Cheshire Cat, she was surprised to find quite a large crowd collected round it: there was a dispute going on between the executioner, the King, and the Queen, who were all talking at once, while all the rest were quite silent, and looked very uncomfortable.
sentences.korean: 체셔 고양이에게 돌아왔을 때, 그녀는 그 주위에 꽤 많은 사람들이 모여 있는 것을 보고 놀랐다. 사형 집행인과 왕, 왕비가 동시에 말을 주고받으며 논쟁을 벌이고 있었고, 나머지 사람들은 모두 조용히 불편한 기색을 보였다.

sentences.english: The moment Alice appeared, she was appealed to by all three to settle the question, and they repeated their arguments to her, though, as they all spoke at once, she found it very hard indeed to make out exactly what they said.
sentences.korean: 앨리스가 나타나자마자 세 사람은 모두 그녀에게 문제를 해결해 달라고 호소했고, 각자의 주장을 반복했지만, 세 사람이 동시에 말하는 바람에 앨리스는 그들이 정확히 무슨 말을 하는지 알아듣기가 매우 어려웠다.

sentences.english: The executioner’s argument was, that you couldn’t cut off a head unless there was a body to cut it off from: that he had never had to do such a thing before, and he wasn’t going to begin at his time of life.
sentences.korean: 사형 집행인의 주장은, 목을 자르려면 몸통이 있어야 한다는 것이었습니다. 그는 이전에 그런 일을 해본 적이 없었고, 지금 나이에 그런 일을 시작할 생각도 없다는 것이었습니다.

sentences.english: The King’s argument was, that anything that had a head could be beheaded, and that you weren’t to talk nonsense.
sentences.korean: 왕의 주장은 머리가 있는 것은 무엇이든 참수할 수 있으며, 허튼소리를 해서는 안 된다는 것이었습니다.

sentences.english: The Queen’s argument was, that if something wasn’t done about it in less than no time she’d have everybody executed, all round.
sentences.korean: 여왕의 주장은, 만약 즉시 조치가 취해지지 않으면 모든 사람을 일괄적으로 처형하겠다는 것이었습니다.

sentences.english: (It was this last remark that had made the whole party look so grave and anxious.)
sentences.korean: (바로 이 마지막 말 때문에 일행 전체의 표정이 그토록 심각하고 불안해 보였던 것이다.)

sentences.english: Alice could think of nothing else to say but “It belongs to the Duchess: you’d better ask her about it.”
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 달리 할 말이 생각나지 않아 "그건 공작부인 거예요. 공작부인에게 물어보는 게 좋겠어요."라고 말했다.

sentences.english: “She’s in prison,” the Queen said to the executioner: “fetch her here.”
sentences.korean: 여왕은 사형 집행인에게 "그녀는 감옥에 있어요. 여기로 데려오세요."라고 말했다.

sentences.english: And the executioner went off like an arrow.
sentences.korean: 그러자 사형 집행인은 화살처럼 달려갔다.

sentences.english: The Cat’s head began fading away the moment he was gone, and, by the time he had come back with the Duchess, it had entirely disappeared; so the King and the executioner ran wildly up and down looking for it, while the rest of the party went back to the game.
sentences.korean: 고양이의 머리는 그가 사라진 순간부터 점점 사라지기 시작했고, 공작부인과 함께 돌아왔을 때는 완전히 사라져 버렸습니다. 그래서 왕과 사형 집행인은 미친 듯이 뛰어다니며 머리를 찾았고, 나머지 사람들은 다시 게임을 계속했습니다.

sentences.english: “You can’t think how glad I am to see you again, you dear old thing!”
sentences.korean: "이 친애하는 할머니, 다시 뵙게 되어 얼마나 기쁜지 몰라요!"

sentences.english: said the Duchess, as she tucked her arm affectionately into Alice’s, and they walked off together.
sentences.korean: 공작부인은 앨리스의 팔에 다정하게 팔짱을 끼며 말했고, 두 사람은 함께 걸어갔다.

sentences.english: Alice was very glad to find her in such a pleasant temper, and thought to herself that perhaps it was only the pepper that had made her so savage when they met in the kitchen.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 그녀가 그렇게 기분 좋은 상태인 것을 보고 매우 기뻤고, 부엌에서 만났을 때 그녀가 그렇게 사나웠던 것은 아마도 후추 때문이었을 거라고 생각했다.

sentences.english: “When I’m a Duchess,” she said to herself, (not in a very hopeful tone though), “I won’t have any pepper in my kitchen at all.
sentences.korean: "내가 공작부인이 되면," 그녀는 (그리 희망적이지 않은 어조로) 혼잣말을 했다. "내 부엌에는 후추가 아예 없을 거야."

sentences.english: Soup does very well without—Maybe it’s always pepper that makes people hot-tempered,” she went on, very much pleased at having found out a new kind of rule, “and vinegar that makes them sour—and camomile that makes them bitter—and—and barley-sugar and such things that make children sweet-tempered.
sentences.korean: 수프는 아무것도 넣지 않아도 아주 맛있어요. 어쩌면 사람들을 화를 나게 하는 건 항상 후추 때문일지도 몰라요.” 그녀는 새로운 규칙을 발견했다는 사실에 매우 만족하며 말을 이었다. “그리고 신맛을 내는 식초, 쓴맛을 내는 캐모마일, 그리고 아이들을 온순하게 만드는 보리 설탕 같은 것들도 마찬가지고요.”

sentences.english: I only wish people knew that: then they wouldn’t be so stingy about it, you know—”
sentences.korean: 사람들이 그걸 알았으면 좋겠어요. 그럼 그렇게 인색하게 굴지 않을 텐데 말이죠."

sentences.english: She had quite forgotten the Duchess by this time, and was a little startled when she heard her voice close to her ear.
sentences.korean: 그녀는 이미 공작부인을 완전히 잊고 있었기에, 가까이서 들려오는 그녀의 목소리에 약간 놀랐다.

sentences.english: “You’re thinking about something, my dear, and that makes you forget to talk.
sentences.korean: "자기야, 뭔가 생각하느라 말하는 걸 잊어버린 것 같아."

sentences.english: I can’t tell you just now what the moral of that is, but I shall remember it in a bit.”
sentences.korean: 지금 당장은 그 교훈이 무엇인지 말씀드릴 수 없지만, 조금 있다가 기억해 두겠습니다.

sentences.english: “Perhaps it hasn’t one,” Alice ventured to remark.
sentences.korean: "어쩌면 아예 없을지도 몰라요." 앨리스가 조심스럽게 말했다.

sentences.english: “Tut, tut, child!”
sentences.korean: “<binary data, 7 bytes> 얘야!”

sentences.english: said the Duchess.
sentences.korean: 공작부인이 말했다.

sentences.english: “Everything’s got a moral, if only you can find it.”
sentences.korean: "모든 것에는 교훈이 담겨 있다. 다만 그 교훈을 찾아낼 수 있을 뿐이다."

sentences.english: And she squeezed herself up closer to Alice’s side as she spoke.
sentences.korean: 그녀는 말을 하면서 앨리스 옆에 더욱 바짝 붙어 붙었다.

sentences.english: Alice did not much like keeping so close to her: first, because the Duchess was very ugly; and secondly, because she was exactly the right height to rest her chin upon Alice’s shoulder, and it was an uncomfortably sharp chin.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 공작부인에게 그렇게 가까이 붙어 있는 것을 별로 좋아하지 않았다. 첫째, 공작부인이 매우 못생겼기 때문이고, 둘째, 공작부인의 턱이 앨리스의 어깨에 딱 맞게 뾰족해서 불편했기 때문이었다.

sentences.english: However, she did not like to be rude, so she bore it as well as she could.
sentences.korean: 하지만 그녀는 무례하게 구는 것을 좋아하지 않았기에 최대한 참아냈다.

sentences.english: “The game’s going on rather better now,” she said, by way of keeping up the conversation a little.
sentences.korean: 그녀는 대화를 이어가려는 듯 "경기가 지금 훨씬 더 잘 진행되고 있어요."라고 말했다.

sentences.english: “’Tis so,” said the Duchess: “and the moral of that is—‘Oh, ’tis love, ’tis love, that makes the world go round!’”
sentences.korean: “맞아요.” 공작부인이 말했다. “그리고 그 교훈은 바로 ‘세상을 움직이는 건 사랑이야!’라는 거죠.”

sentences.english: “Somebody said,” Alice whispered, “that it’s done by everybody minding their own business!”
sentences.korean: “누군가 그러더라,” 앨리스가 속삭였다. “모두가 자기 일에만 신경 쓰면 그렇게 되는 거라고!”

sentences.english: “Ah, well!
sentences.korean: 아, 그렇군요!

sentences.english: It means much the same thing,” said the Duchess, digging her sharp little chin into Alice’s shoulder as she added, “and the moral of that is—‘Take care of the sense, and the sounds will take care of themselves.’”
sentences.korean: "그건 거의 같은 의미야." 공작부인은 뾰족한 작은 턱을 앨리스의 어깨에 파묻으며 덧붙였다. "그리고 그 교훈은 '의미를 잘 살피면 소리는 저절로 따라온다'는 거지."

sentences.english: “How fond she is of finding morals in things!”
sentences.korean: "그녀는 모든 것에서 도덕적인 면을 찾아내는 걸 얼마나 좋아하는지!"

sentences.english: Alice thought to herself.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 속으로 생각했다.

sentences.english: “I dare say you’re wondering why I don’t put my arm round your waist,” the Duchess said after a pause: “the reason is, that I’m doubtful about the temper of your flamingo.
sentences.korean: "제가 왜 당신의 허리에 팔을 두르지 않는지 궁금하시겠죠?" 공작부인은 잠시 말을 멈춘 후 말했다. "그 이유는 당신의 플라밍고의 성격이 어떨지 확신이 서지 않기 때문입니다."

sentences.english: Shall I try the experiment?”
sentences.korean: 제가 그 실험을 해볼까요?

sentences.english: “He might bite,” Alice cautiously replied, not feeling at all anxious to have the experiment tried.
sentences.korean: "물어뜯을지도 몰라요." 앨리스는 조심스럽게 대답하며, 그 실험을 시도하는 것에 전혀 불안감을 느끼지 않았다.

sentences.english: “Very true,” said the Duchess: “flamingoes and mustard both bite.
sentences.korean: "정말 그래요." 공작부인이 말했다. "플라밍고와 겨자 둘 다 맵죠."

sentences.english: And the moral of that is—‘Birds of a feather flock together.’”
sentences.korean: 그리고 그 교훈은 '유유상종'이라는 것이다."

sentences.english: “Only mustard isn’t a bird,” Alice remarked.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 "겨자만 새가 아니네."라고 말했다.

sentences.english: “Right, as usual,” said the Duchess: “what a clear way you have of putting things!”
sentences.korean: "맞아요, 늘 그렇듯," 공작부인이 말했다. "정말 명확하게 표현하시네요!"

sentences.english: “It’s a mineral, I think,” said Alice.
sentences.korean: “제 생각엔 광물 같아요.”라고 앨리스가 말했다.

sentences.english: “Of course it is,” said the Duchess, who seemed ready to agree to everything that Alice said; “there’s a large mustard-mine near here.
sentences.korean: "당연하지." 앨리스의 말에 모두 동의할 것처럼 보이는 공작부인이 말했다. "이 근처에 큰 겨자 광산이 있거든."

sentences.english: And the moral of that is—‘The more there is of mine, the less there is of yours.’”
sentences.korean: 그리고 그 교훈은 ‘내 것이 많을수록 네 것은 적어진다’는 것이다.”

sentences.english: “Oh, I know!”
sentences.korean: “아, 저도 알아요!”

sentences.english: exclaimed Alice, who had not attended to this last remark, “it’s a vegetable.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 마지막 말을 제대로 듣지 못하고 있다가 "채소잖아!"라고 소리쳤다.

sentences.english: It doesn’t look like one, but it is.”
sentences.korean: 겉보기엔 그렇지 않지만, 사실입니다.

sentences.english: “I quite agree with you,” said the Duchess; “and the moral of that is—‘Be what you would seem to be’—or if you’d like it put more simply—‘Never imagine yourself not to be otherwise than what it might appear to others that what you were or might have been was not otherwise than what you had been would have appeared to them to be otherwise.’”
sentences.korean: "전적으로 동감합니다." 공작부인이 말했다. "그 말씀의 교훈은 '남들이 보기에 당신이 어떤 사람인지 그대로 보여라'라는 것이죠. 좀 더 간단히 말하자면, '당신이 과거에 어떤 사람이었는지, 혹은 어떤 사람이었을지도 모른다는 사실이 남들에게 어떻게 비춰질지 상상하지 마라'는 겁니다."

sentences.english: “I think I should understand that better,” Alice said very politely, “if I had it written down: but I can’t quite follow it as you say it.”
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 아주 공손하게 말했다. "글로 적어 놓으면 더 잘 이해할 수 있을 것 같아요. 말씀하시는 대로 하니까 잘 안 되네요."

sentences.english: “That’s nothing to what I could say if I chose,” the Duchess replied, in a pleased tone.
sentences.korean: "제가 마음만 먹으면 할 수 있는 말에 비하면 아무것도 아니죠." 공작부인은 만족스러운 어조로 대답했다.

sentences.english: “Pray don’t trouble yourself to say it any longer than that,” said Alice.
sentences.korean: “제발 더 길게 말씀하지 않으셔도 돼요.” 앨리스가 말했다.

sentences.english: “Oh, don’t talk about trouble!”
sentences.korean: “아, 문제 얘기는 꺼내지 마!”

sentences.english: said the Duchess.
sentences.korean: 공작부인이 말했다.

sentences.english: “I make you a present of everything I’ve said as yet.”
sentences.korean: “제가 지금까지 했던 모든 말을 당신에게 선물로 드립니다.”

sentences.english: “A cheap sort of present!”
sentences.korean: "저렴한 선물이네요!"

sentences.english: thought Alice.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 생각했다.

sentences.english: “I’m glad they don’t give birthday presents like that!”
sentences.korean: "그런 생일 선물을 안 줘서 다행이야!"

sentences.english: But she did not venture to say it out loud.
sentences.korean: 하지만 그녀는 감히 그 말을 입 밖으로 꺼내지 못했다.

sentences.english: “Thinking again?”
sentences.korean: “다시 생각해 보시겠어요?”

sentences.english: the Duchess asked, with another dig of her sharp little chin.
sentences.korean: 공작부인은 날카로운 작은 턱을 다시 한번 찡그리며 물었다.

sentences.english: “I’ve a right to think,” said Alice sharply, for she was beginning to feel a little worried.
sentences.korean: "저도 생각할 권리가 있어요." 앨리스는 날카롭게 말했다. 그녀는 약간 걱정이 되기 시작했기 때문이다.

sentences.english: “Just about as much right,” said the Duchess, “as pigs have to fly; and the m—”
sentences.korean: "돼지가 하늘을 날 권리가 있는 것과 마찬가지죠." 공작부인이 말했다. "그리고 그 여자는..."

sentences.english: But here, to Alice’s great surprise, the Duchess’s voice died away, even in the middle of her favourite word ‘moral,’ and the arm that was linked into hers began to tremble.
sentences.korean: 하지만 앨리스는 놀랍게도 공작부인의 목소리가 그녀가 가장 좋아하는 단어인 '도덕'을 말하는 도중에 갑자기 잦아들었고, 그녀의 팔에 얽혀 있던 팔이 떨리기 시작했다.

sentences.english: Alice looked up, and there stood the Queen in front of them, with her arms folded, frowning like a thunderstorm.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 고개를 들었고, 그곳에는 여왕이 팔짱을 끼고 폭풍우처럼 찡그린 얼굴로 그들 앞에 서 있었다.

sentences.english: “A fine day, your Majesty!”
sentences.korean: "날씨가 참 좋으시군요, 폐하!"

sentences.english: the Duchess began in a low, weak voice.
sentences.korean: 공작부인은 낮고 힘없는 목소리로 말을 시작했다.

sentences.english: “Now, I give you fair warning,” shouted the Queen, stamping on the ground as she spoke; “either you or your head must be off, and that in about half no time!
sentences.korean: 여왕은 땅을 쿵쿵 구르며 소리쳤다. "자, 이제 경고하는데, 너 아니면 네 목이 잘릴 거야. 그것도 아주 순식간에 말이지!"

sentences.english: Take your choice!”
sentences.korean: 선택하세요!

sentences.english: The Duchess took her choice, and was gone in a moment.
sentences.korean: 공작부인은 선택을 하고는 순식간에 사라졌다.

sentences.english: “Let’s go on with the game,” the Queen said to Alice; and Alice was too much frightened to say a word, but slowly followed her back to the croquet-ground.
sentences.korean: “자, 게임을 계속하자.” 여왕이 앨리스에게 말했다. 앨리스는 너무 무서워서 한마디도 할 수 없었지만, 천천히 여왕을 따라 크로케 경기장으로 돌아갔다.

sentences.english: The other guests had taken advantage of the Queen’s absence, and were resting in the shade: however, the moment they saw her, they hurried back to the game, the Queen merely remarking that a moment’s delay would cost them their lives.
sentences.korean: 다른 손님들은 여왕이 자리를 비운 틈을 타 그늘에서 쉬고 있었지만, 여왕을 보자마자 서둘러 경기로 돌아갔다. 여왕은 잠시라도 지체하면 목숨을 잃을 수도 있다고 한마디만 했다.

sentences.english: All the time they were playing the Queen never left off quarrelling with the other players, and shouting “Off with his head!”
sentences.korean: 게임을 하는 내내 여왕은 다른 플레이어들과 끊임없이 다투고 "저놈의 목을 베어라!"라고 소리쳤다.

sentences.english: or “Off with her head!”
sentences.korean: 또는 “목을 베어라!”

sentences.english: Those whom she sentenced were taken into custody by the soldiers, who of course had to leave off being arches to do this, so that by the end of half an hour or so there were no arches left, and all the players, except the King, the Queen, and Alice, were in custody and under sentence of execution.
sentences.korean: 그녀가 사형을 선고한 사람들은 병사들에게 체포되었는데, 병사들은 당연히 그 일을 하기 위해 아치 역할을 그만둬야 했다. 그래서 30분쯤 지나자 아치는 하나도 남지 않았고, 왕과 왕비, 앨리스를 제외한 모든 배우들은 체포되어 사형 선고를 받게 되었다.

sentences.english: Then the Queen left off, quite out of breath, and said to Alice, “Have you seen the Mock Turtle yet?”
sentences.korean: 그러자 여왕은 숨이 턱까지 차서 말을 멈추고 앨리스에게 "가짜 거북이를 봤니?"라고 물었다.

sentences.english: “No,” said Alice.
sentences.korean: “아니요.” 앨리스가 말했다.

sentences.english: “I don’t even know what a Mock Turtle is.”
sentences.korean: "모크 터틀이 뭔지도 모르겠어요."

sentences.english: “It’s the thing Mock Turtle Soup is made from,” said the Queen.
sentences.korean: "그건 바로 가짜 거북이 수프를 만드는 재료예요."라고 여왕이 말했다.

sentences.english: “I never saw one, or heard of one,” said Alice.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 "본 적도 없고, 들어본 적도 없어요."라고 말했다.

sentences.english: “Come on, then,” said the Queen, “and he shall tell you his history.”
sentences.korean: “자, 어서 오세요.” 여왕이 말했다. “그가 자신의 이야기를 들려줄 겁니다.”

sentences.english: As they walked off together, Alice heard the King say in a low voice, to the company generally, “You are all pardoned.”
sentences.korean: 그들이 함께 걸어가는 동안 앨리스는 왕이 낮은 목소리로 일행 전체에게 "여러분 모두 사면되었습니다."라고 말하는 것을 들었다.

sentences.english: “Come, that’s a good thing!”
sentences.korean: "이봐, 그건 좋은 일이야!"

sentences.english: she said to herself, for she had felt quite unhappy at the number of executions the Queen had ordered.
sentences.korean: 그녀는 여왕이 명령한 사형 집행 건수가 너무 많아 몹시 불쾌했기에 속으로 그렇게 말했다.

sentences.english: They very soon came upon a Gryphon, lying fast asleep in the sun.
sentences.korean: 그들은 곧 햇볕 아래서 곤히 잠들어 있는 그리핀을 발견했다.

sentences.english: (If you don’t know what a Gryphon is, look at the picture.)
sentences.korean: (그리핀이 뭔지 모르시면 사진을 보세요.)

sentences.english: “Up, lazy thing!”
sentences.korean: “일어나라, 게으름뱅이!”

sentences.english: said the Queen, “and take this young lady to see the Mock Turtle, and to hear his history.
sentences.korean: 여왕이 말했다. "그리고 이 아가씨를 데리고 가짜 거북이를 만나러 가서 그의 이야기를 들어보게 하세요."

sentences.english: I must go back and see after some executions I have ordered;” and she walked off, leaving Alice alone with the Gryphon.
sentences.korean: "내가 명령한 처형 몇 건을 확인하고 돌아가 봐야겠어." 그녀는 그렇게 말하고는 앨리스를 그리핀과 단둘이 남겨둔 채 걸어갔다.

sentences.english: Alice did not quite like the look of the creature, but on the whole she thought it would be quite as safe to stay with it as to go after that savage Queen: so she waited.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 그 생물의 생김새가 그다지 마음에 들지는 않았지만, 사나운 여왕을 쫓아가는 것보다는 그 생물과 함께 있는 것이 안전할 거라고 생각해서 기다렸다.

sentences.english: The Gryphon sat up and rubbed its eyes: then it watched the Queen till she was out of sight: then it chuckled.
sentences.korean: 그리핀은 몸을 일으켜 눈을 비볐다. 그리고 여왕이 시야에서 사라질 때까지 지켜보다가 낄낄거렸다.

sentences.english: “What fun!”
sentences.korean: "정말 재밌네요!"

sentences.english: said the Gryphon, half to itself, half to Alice.
sentences.korean: 그리폰은 혼잣말처럼, 앨리스에게 말하듯이 말했다.

sentences.english: “What is the fun?”
sentences.korean: “무슨 재미가 있겠어?”

sentences.english: said Alice.
sentences.korean: 앨리스가 말했다.

sentences.english: “Why, she,” said the Gryphon.
sentences.korean: "왜 하필 그녀지?" 그리폰이 말했다.

sentences.english: “It’s all her fancy, that: they never executes nobody, you know.
sentences.korean: "그건 다 그녀의 상상일 뿐이야. 그들은 절대 아무도 처형하지 않아."

sentences.english: Come on!”
sentences.korean: 어서 해봐요!"

sentences.english: “Everybody says ‘come on!’
sentences.korean: "모두가 '어서 와!'라고 말하죠."

sentences.english: here,” thought Alice, as she went slowly after it: “I never was so ordered about in all my life, never!”
sentences.korean: "여기야," 앨리스는 천천히 그것을 따라가면서 생각했다. "내 평생 이렇게 명령받은 적은 한 번도 없었어, 정말!"

sentences.english: They had not gone far before they saw the Mock Turtle in the distance, sitting sad and lonely on a little ledge of rock, and, as they came nearer, Alice could hear him sighing as if his heart would break.
sentences.korean: 그들은 얼마 가지 않아 멀리 바위 턱에 슬프고 외롭게 앉아 있는 가짜 거북을 발견했고, 가까이 다가가자 앨리스는 마치 심장이 찢어질 듯 한숨 쉬는 가짜 거북의 소리를 들을 수 있었다.

sentences.english: She pitied him deeply.
sentences.korean: 그녀는 그를 몹시 불쌍히 여겼다.

sentences.english: “What is his sorrow?”
sentences.korean: “그의 슬픔은 무엇인가?”

sentences.english: she asked the Gryphon, and the Gryphon answered, very nearly in the same words as before, “It’s all his fancy, that: he hasn’t got no sorrow, you know.
sentences.korean: 그녀가 그리폰에게 묻자, 그리폰은 이전과 거의 같은 말로 대답했다. "그건 전부 그의 상상일 뿐이야. 그는 슬픔 같은 건 전혀 없단다."

sentences.english: Come on!”
sentences.korean: 어서 해봐요!"

sentences.english: So they went up to the Mock Turtle, who looked at them with large eyes full of tears, but said nothing.
sentences.korean: 그래서 그들은 가짜 거북에게 다가갔고, 가짜 거북은 눈물이 가득 찬 커다란 눈으로 그들을 바라보았지만 아무 말도 하지 않았다.

sentences.english: “This here young lady,” said the Gryphon, “she wants for to know your history, she do.”
sentences.korean: 그리핀이 말했다. "저 아가씨는 당신의 과거에 대해 알고 싶어해요."

sentences.english: “I’ll tell it her,” said the Mock Turtle in a deep, hollow tone: “sit down, both of you, and don’t speak a word till I’ve finished.”
sentences.korean: 가짜 거북이는 깊고 공허한 목소리로 “내가 그녀에게 말해줄게. 둘 다 앉아. 내가 끝낼 때까지 한 마디도 하지 마.”라고 말했다.

sentences.english: So they sat down, and nobody spoke for some minutes.
sentences.korean: 그래서 그들은 자리에 앉았고, 몇 분 동안 아무도 말을 하지 않았다.

sentences.english: Alice thought to herself, “I don’t see how he can ever finish, if he doesn’t begin.”
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 속으로 생각했다. "시작하지 않으면 어떻게 끝낼 수 있겠어?"

sentences.english: But she waited patiently.
sentences.korean: 하지만 그녀는 인내심을 갖고 기다렸다.

sentences.english: “Once,” said the Mock Turtle at last, with a deep sigh, “I was a real Turtle.”
sentences.korean: 가짜 거북이는 마침내 깊은 한숨을 쉬며 “한때는 나도 진짜 거북이였지.”라고 말했다.

sentences.english: These words were followed by a very long silence, broken only by an occasional exclamation of “Hjckrrh!”
sentences.korean: 이 말 이후로 아주 긴 침묵이 흘렀고, 간간이 "흐흐르!" 하는 감탄사만이 그 침묵을 깨뜨렸다.

sentences.english: from the Gryphon, and the constant heavy sobbing of the Mock Turtle.
sentences.korean: 그리핀의 울음소리와 가짜 거북이의 끊임없는 흐느낌 소리가 들렸다.

sentences.english: Alice was very nearly getting up and saying, “Thank you, sir, for your interesting story,” but she could not help thinking there must be more to come, so she sat still and said nothing.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 거의 자리에서 일어나 "흥미로운 이야기 감사합니다, 선생님"이라고 말할 뻔했지만, 앞으로 더 많은 이야기가 나올 것 같다는 생각이 자꾸 들어서 가만히 앉아 아무 말도 하지 않았다.

sentences.english: “When we were little,” the Mock Turtle went on at last, more calmly, though still sobbing a little now and then, “we went to school in the sea.
sentences.korean: 가짜 거북은 마침내 좀 더 차분한 목소리로, 비록 여전히 간간이 흐느끼긴 했지만, 말을 이었다. "우리가 어렸을 때, 우리는 바다에서 학교에 다녔단다."

sentences.english: The master was an old Turtle—we used to call him Tortoise—”
sentences.korean: 주인님은 늙은 거북이였는데, 우리는 그분을 거북이라고 불렀죠."

sentences.english: “Why did you call him Tortoise, if he wasn’t one?”
sentences.korean: "그가 거북이가 아닌데 왜 이름을 거북이라고 지었어?"

sentences.english: Alice asked.
sentences.korean: 앨리스가 물었다.

sentences.english: “We called him Tortoise because he taught us,” said the Mock Turtle angrily: “really you are very dull!”
sentences.korean: "우리가 그를 거북이라고 부른 건 그가 우리에게 가르쳐줬기 때문이야." 가짜 거북이가 화를 내며 말했다. "정말 너희들은 너무 둔해!"

sentences.english: “You ought to be ashamed of yourself for asking such a simple question,” added the Gryphon; and then they both sat silent and looked at poor Alice, who felt ready to sink into the earth.
sentences.korean: "그렇게 간단한 질문을 하다니 부끄러운 줄 알아야지." 그리핀이 덧붙였다. 그러자 둘은 아무 말 없이 불쌍한 앨리스를 바라보았다. 앨리스는 땅속으로라도 가라앉고 싶은 심정이었다.

sentences.english: At last the Gryphon said to the Mock Turtle, “Drive on, old fellow!
sentences.korean: 마침내 그리폰이 가짜 거북이에게 “계속 가자, 친구!”라고 말했다.

sentences.english: Don’t be all day about it!”
sentences.korean: 하루 종일 그 일에 매달리지 마세요!

sentences.english: and he went on in these words:
sentences.korean: 그리고 그는 다음과 같이 말을 이었다.

sentences.english: “Yes, we went to school in the sea, though you mayn’t believe it—”
sentences.korean: "네, 믿기 어려우시겠지만 저희는 바다에서 학교를 다녔어요."

sentences.english: “I never said I didn’t!”
sentences.korean: “내가 안 그랬다고 말한 적은 없잖아!”

sentences.english: interrupted Alice.
sentences.korean: 앨리스가 말을 끊었다.

sentences.english: “You did,” said the Mock Turtle.
sentences.korean: “네가 그랬잖아.” 가짜 거북이가 말했다.

sentences.english: “Hold your tongue!”
sentences.korean: “입 다물어!”

sentences.english: added the Gryphon, before Alice could speak again.
sentences.korean: 앨리스가 다시 말을 꺼내기도 전에 그리핀이 덧붙였다.

sentences.english: The Mock Turtle went on.
sentences.korean: 가짜 거북이는 계속 말을 이었다.

sentences.english: “We had the best of educations—in fact, we went to school every day—”
sentences.korean: “우리는 최고의 교육을 받았어요. 사실, 매일 학교에 갔죠.”

sentences.english: “I’ve been to a day-school, too,” said Alice; “you needn’t be so proud as all that.”
sentences.korean: “저도 사립학교에 다녀봤어요.” 앨리스가 말했다. “그렇게까지 자랑스러워할 필요는 없어요.”

sentences.english: “With extras?”

sentences.english: “Yes,” said Alice, “we learned French and music.”
sentences.korean: “네,” 앨리스가 말했다. “저희는 프랑스어와 음악을 배웠어요.”

sentences.english: “And washing?”

sentences.english: “Certainly not!”
sentences.korean: “절대 아니에요!”

sentences.english: said Alice indignantly.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 분개하며 말했다.

sentences.english: “Ah!
then yours wasn’t a really good school,” said the Mock Turtle in a tone of great relief.
sentences.korean: "그럼 네 학교는 그다지 좋은 학교가 아니었겠네." 가짜 거북이가 안도의 한숨을 쉬며 말했다.

sentences.english: “Now at ours they had at the end of the bill, ‘French, music, and washing—extra.’”
sentences.korean: "우리 가게에서는 계산서 맨 끝에 '프랑스어, 음악, 세탁 - 추가 요금'이라고 적혀 있었어요."

sentences.english: “You couldn’t have wanted it much,” said Alice; “living at the bottom of the sea.”
sentences.korean: "바다 밑바닥에서 사는 걸 그렇게 원했을 리는 없겠죠." 앨리스가 말했다.

sentences.english: “I couldn’t afford to learn it.” said the Mock Turtle with a sigh.
sentences.korean: “배울 형편이 안 됐어.” 가짜 거북이가 한숨을 쉬며 말했다.

sentences.english: “I only took the regular course.”
sentences.korean: “저는 정규 과정만 수강했어요.”

sentences.english: “What was that?”
sentences.korean: "방금 뭐라고 했어?"

sentences.korean: 가짜 거북이는 "물론 처음에는 휘청거리고 몸부림치는 것이겠죠."라고 대답했다. "그리고 나서 산수의 여러 갈래, 즉 야망, 산만함, 추함, 조롱이 있겠죠."

sentences.english: “I never heard of ‘Uglification,’” Alice ventured to say.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 "저는 '추화'라는 말은 처음 들어봤어요."라고 조심스럽게 말했다.

sentences.english: “What is it?”
sentences.korean: “그게 뭐예요?”

sentences.english: The Gryphon lifted up both its paws in surprise.
sentences.korean: 그리핀은 놀라서 두 발을 번쩍 들었다.

sentences.english: “What!
sentences.korean: "무엇!

sentences.english: Never heard of uglifying!”
sentences.korean: 못생기게 만든다는 말은 처음 들어봐요!

sentences.english: it exclaimed.
sentences.korean: 그것은 소리쳤다.

sentences.english: “You know what to beautify is, I suppose?”

sentences.english: Alice did not feel encouraged to ask any more questions about it, so she turned to the Mock Turtle, and said “What else had you to learn?”

sentences.english: “Well, there was Mystery,” the Mock Turtle replied, counting off the subjects on his flappers, “—Mystery, ancient and modern, with Seaography: then Drawling—the Drawling-master was an old conger-eel, that used to come once a week: he taught us Drawling, Stretching, and Fainting in Coils.”
sentences.korean: “음, 신비 수업이 있었지.” 가짜 거북이가 지느러미로 과목들을 하나씩 세며 대답했다. “고대와 현대의 신비 수업, 해양학도 있었고, 그다음엔 느릿느릿 말하기 수업이 있었는데, 느릿느릿 말하기 선생님은 일주일에 한 번씩 오시는 늙은 곰치였어. 그분은 우리에게 느릿느릿 말하기, 스트레칭, 그리고 몸을 웅크리고 기절하는 법을 가르쳐 주셨지.”

sentences.english: “What was that like?”

sentences.english: said Alice.

sentences.english: And the Gryphon never learnt it.”

sentences.english: He was an old crab, he was.”
sentences.korean: 그는 늙은 게였어.

sentences.english: “I never went to him,” the Mock Turtle said with a sigh: “he taught Laughing and Grief, they used to say.”

sentences.english: “So he did, so he did,” said the Gryphon, sighing in his turn; and both creatures hid their faces in their paws.

sentences.english: “And how many hours a day did you do lessons?”

sentences.english: said Alice, in a hurry to change the subject.

sentences.english: “Ten hours the first day,” said the Mock Turtle: “nine the next, and so on.”
sentences.korean: 가짜 거북이는 “첫날은 10시간, 다음 날은 9시간, 이런 식으로 계속하면 된다”라고 말했다.

sentences.english: “What a curious plan!”

sentences.korean: 앨리스는 소리쳤다.

sentences.english: “That’s the reason they’re called lessons,” the Gryphon remarked: “because they lessen from day to day.”

sentences.english: This was quite a new idea to Alice, and she thought it over a little before she made her next remark.

sentences.english: “Then the eleventh day must have been a holiday?”

sentences.korean: "당연하지," 가짜 거북이가 말했다.

sentences.english: “And how did you manage on the twelfth?”
sentences.korean: “그럼 12일은 어떻게 보내셨어요?”

sentences.english: Alice went on eagerly.
sentences.korean: 앨리스는 열정적으로 말을 이었다.

sentences.english: “That’s enough about lessons,” the Gryphon interrupted in a very decided tone: “tell her something about the games now.”

sentences.english: The Mock Turtle sighed deeply, and drew the back of one flapper across his eyes.
sentences.korean: 가짜 거북은 깊은 한숨을 쉬고는 지느러미 한쪽 뒷부분으로 눈을 가렸다.

sentences.english: He looked at Alice, and tried to speak, but for a minute or two sobs choked his voice.
sentences.korean: 그는 앨리스를 바라보며 말을 하려 했지만, 1~2분 동안 흐느낌 때문에 목소리가 나오지 않았다.

sentences.english: “Same as if he had a bone in his throat,” said the Gryphon: and it set to work shaking him and punching him in the back.
sentences.korean: "마치 목에 뼈가 걸린 것 같군." 그리핀이 말하며 그를 흔들고 등을 주먹으로 치기 시작했다.

sentences.english: At last the Mock Turtle recovered his voice, and, with tears running down his cheeks, he went on again:—
sentences.korean: 마침내 가짜 거북이는 목소리를 되찾았고, 눈물을 흘리며 다시 말을 이어갔다.

sentences.english: “You may not have lived much under the sea—” (“I haven’t,” said Alice)—“and perhaps you were never even introduced to a lobster—” (Alice began to say “I once tasted—” but checked herself hastily, and said “No, never”) “—so you can have no idea what a delightful thing a Lobster Quadrille is!”
sentences.korean: "바닷속에서 오래 살아보지 못했을 수도 있고—" ("네," 앨리스가 말했다.) "아마 바닷가재를 접해본 적도 없을 거예요—" (앨리스는 "한번 맛본 적은 있어요—"라고 말하려다 재빨리 말을 멈추고 "아니요, 전혀요.") "—그러니 바닷가재 쿼드릴이 얼마나 즐거운 것인지 전혀 모르실 거예요!"

sentences.english: “No, indeed,” said Alice.
sentences.korean: “아니요, 정말 그래요.” 앨리스가 말했다.

sentences.english: “What sort of a dance is it?”
sentences.korean: “이건 무슨 종류의 춤인가요?”

sentences.english: “Why,” said the Gryphon, “you first form into a line along the sea-shore—”
sentences.korean: 그리폰이 말했다. "왜, 너희는 먼저 해안선을 따라 일렬로 늘어서는 거지?"

sentences.english: “Two lines!”
sentences.korean: "두 줄!"

sentences.english: cried the Mock Turtle.
sentences.korean: 가짜 거북이가 울었다.

sentences.english: “Seals, turtles, salmon, and so on; then, when you’ve cleared all the jelly-fish out of the way—”
sentences.korean: "물개, 거북이, 연어 등등이 있고, 그런 다음 해파리를 모두 치우고 나면—"

sentences.english: “That generally takes some time,” interrupted the Gryphon.
sentences.korean: "그건 보통 시간이 좀 걸리죠." 그리핀이 말을 끊었다.

sentences.english: “—you advance twice—”
sentences.korean: "—두 번 전진합니다—"

sentences.english: “Each with a lobster as a partner!”
sentences.korean: "각자 랍스터를 파트너로 삼아!"

sentences.english: cried the Gryphon.
sentences.korean: 그리핀이 소리쳤다.

sentences.english: “Of course,” the Mock Turtle said: “advance twice, set to partners—”
sentences.korean: "물론이지." 가짜 거북이가 말했다. "두 번 전진하고, 파트너를 정해—"

sentences.english: “—change lobsters, and retire in same order,” continued the Gryphon.
sentences.korean: "랍스터를 바꾸고, 같은 순서로 은퇴하세요." 그리폰이 말을 이었다.

sentences.english: “Then, you know,” the Mock Turtle went on, “you throw the—”
sentences.korean: “그러면, 알잖아,” 가짜 거북이가 말을 이었다. “던지면—”

sentences.english: “The lobsters!”
sentences.korean: “랍스터요!”

sentences.english: shouted the Gryphon, with a bound into the air.
sentences.korean: 그리핀은 공중으로 뛰어오르며 소리쳤다.

sentences.english: “—as far out to sea as you can—”
sentences.korean: "—가능한 한 멀리 바다로—"

sentences.english: “Swim after them!”
sentences.korean: "그들을 따라 헤엄쳐 가세요!"

sentences.english: screamed the Gryphon.
sentences.korean: 그리핀이 비명을 질렀다.

sentences.english: “Turn a somersault in the sea!”
sentences.korean: 바다에서 공중제비를 해 봐!

sentences.english: cried the Mock Turtle, capering wildly about.
sentences.korean: 가짜 거북이는 미친 듯이 뛰어다니며 소리쳤다.

sentences.english: “Change lobsters again!”
sentences.korean: “랍스터를 다시 바꿔주세요!”

sentences.english: yelled the Gryphon at the top of its voice.

sentences.english: “Back to land again, and that’s all the first figure,” said the Mock Turtle, suddenly dropping his voice; and the two creatures, who had been jumping about like mad things all this time, sat down again very sadly and quietly, and looked at Alice.
sentences.korean: “다시 육지로 돌아가는 거야, 그게 전부야, 첫 번째 그림아.” 가짜 거북이가 갑자기 목소리를 낮추며 말했다. 그러자 그동안 미친 듯이 뛰어다니던 두 생물은 다시 아주 슬프고 조용히 자리에 앉아 앨리스를 바라보았다.

sentences.english: “It must be a very pretty dance,” said Alice timidly.
sentences.korean: "정말 아름다운 춤일 거예요." 앨리스가 수줍게 말했다.

sentences.english: “Would you like to see a little of it?”
sentences.korean: “조금만 보시겠어요?”

sentences.english: said the Mock Turtle.
sentences.korean: 가짜 거북이가 말했다.

sentences.english: “Very much indeed,” said Alice.
sentences.korean: “정말 그래요.” 앨리스가 말했다.

sentences.english: “We can do without lobsters, you know.

sentences.english: So they began solemnly dancing round and round Alice, every now and then treading on her toes when they passed too close, and waving their forepaws to mark the time, while the Mock Turtle sang this, very slowly and sadly:—

sentences.english: “Will you walk a little faster?”

sentences.english: “There’s a porpoise close behind us, and he’s treading on my tail.
sentences.korean: "바로 뒤에 돌고래 한 마리가 있는데, 내 꼬리를 밟고 있어요."

sentences.english: They are waiting on the shingle—will you come and join the dance?

sentences.english: Will you, won’t you, will you, won’t you, will you join the dance?

sentences.english: “You can really have no notion how delightful it will be When they take us up and throw us, with the lobsters, out to sea!”
sentences.korean: "우리가 배에 올라타서 바닷가재와 함께 바다로 던져질 때 얼마나 즐거울지 당신은 정말 상상도 못 할 거예요!"

sentences.english: But the snail replied “Too far, too far!”

sentences.english: Will you, won’t you, will you, won’t you, will you join the dance?
sentences.korean: 춤에 함께 하실 건가요, 안 하실 건가요, 함께 하실 건가요, 안 하실 건가요, 함께 하실 건가요?

sentences.english: “Thank you, it’s a very interesting dance to watch,” said Alice, feeling very glad that it was over at last: “and I do so like that curious song about the whiting!”

sentences.english: “Oh, as to the whiting,” said the Mock Turtle, “they—you’ve seen them, of course?”

sentences.english: “Yes,” said Alice, “I’ve often seen them at dinn—” she checked herself hastily.

sentences.english: “I don’t know where Dinn may be,” said the Mock Turtle, “but if you’ve seen them so often, of course you know what they’re like.”

sentences.english: “I believe so,” Alice replied thoughtfully.
sentences.korean: "그렇게 생각해요." 앨리스는 생각에 잠긴 듯 대답했다.

sentences.english: “They have their tails in their mouths—and they’re all over crumbs.”

sentences.english: “You’re wrong about the crumbs,” said the Mock Turtle: “crumbs would all wash off in the sea.
